articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Espanyol vs Elche
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Espanyol y al Elche en el RCDE Stadium correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Espanyol y al Elche en el RCDE Stadium correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Espanyol recibe al Elche este viernes en el RCDE Stadium, en el partido correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga 26/27. El conjunto de Manolo González llega a este compromiso en un buen momento de forma, tras conquistar El Sadar con un contundente 0-2 ante el Osasuna gracias al doblete de Roberto Fernández, resultado que corta una racha de tres jornadas sin ganar y que sitúa a los pericos en puestos de acceso a competición europea. Favorito para el partido entre Espanyol y Elche Por su parte, el Elche llega a Barcelona todavía sin conocer la victoria en LaLiga. El conjunto de Martín Anselmi empató 1-1 en San Mamés ante el Athletic Club en su última salida, un resultado que le permite sumar su tercer punto de la temporada pero que no despeja las dudas sobre un equipo que sigue siendo el que más goles ha encajado del campeonato, con una media de 2,6 tantos en contra por partido en lo que va de curso. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Espanyol, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia dado el buen nivel competitivo mostrado por el Elche en sus últimas salidas. Codere paga la victoria local a cuota 1.90, por 3.30 del empate y 3.6 de la victoria del cuadro ilicitano. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Espanyol solo ha mantenido su portería a cero en una ocasión esta temporada, mientras que el Elche ha encajado en la práctica totalidad de sus partidos disputados, aunque también ha demostrado capacidad para ver puerta, como quedó patente ante el Athletic. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es la misma que la del caso contrario. Codere paga a 1.85 el "sí" y a 1.85 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con una producción ofensiva equilibrada. El Elche acumula la peor defensa de LaLiga, con más de dos goles en contra de media por partido, mientras que el Espanyol ha demostrado en las últimas jornadas que puede resolver los partidos con contundencia cuando encuentra los espacios. Con estos datos, Codere sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 2.05, por 1.72 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Espanyol, con un juego intenso por bandas y buscando siempre la posesión en campo rival, suele generar un volumen alto de saques de esquina jugando en el RCDE Stadium. El Elche, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus últimas salidas serias dificultades para sostener el balón en campo contrario, lo que invita a pensar en una notable diferencia de córners a favor del conjunto local en este duelo.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Tremors shake athletes awake
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: BENGALURU: Several members of the Indian athletics contingent training in Tsukuba City, ahead of the Asian Games beginning in Nagoya on Saturday, rush.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Several members of the Indian athletics contingent training in Tsukuba City, ahead of the Asian Games beginning in Nagoya on Saturday, rushed out of their hotel rooms on Wednesday night after a tremor shook them from their sleep.While some athletes thought it was a dream, few others shared that they felt someone had barged into their room and begun shaking their bed.“It was a real scare for many of the athletes as their beds began to shake and hit the wall. Many ran out of their rooms and gathered in the corridor, while a few others learned about the tremor only at the breakfast table,” sources told TOI.“There is no damage but it lasted for around 30-60 seconds and the hotel was shaking vigorously,” they added.The earthquake that hit the Tsukuba region on Wednesday night had a magnitude of 5.0 on the Mw scale. Nagoya experienced heavy rains last week, and Typoon Dujuan is expected to hit the coastline on Monday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games: Mismanagement continues as Indian gymnast Pranati Nayak, coach allotted same room on cruise ship
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: A room mix-up, hours of uncertainty and a missing letter in official paperwork, Indian gymnast Pranati Nayak and her coach Ashok Mishra endured a late.
articles.body: A room mix-up, hours of uncertainty and a missing letter in official paperwork, Indian gymnast Pranati Nayak and her coach Ashok Mishra endured a late-night accommodation ordeal at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.The duo were mistakenly assigned the same room aboard a cruise ship being used to accommodate the Indian contingent, triggering concerns over the mixed-gender arrangement. The issue was resolved only after the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) intervened, with alternative accommodation finalised around 1:30 am on Thursday.However, the ordeal continued when Mishra went to collect the keys to his separate room, only to be told that his booking could not be found in the hotel register.IOA intervention resolves room mix-up after midnightAccording to NDTV, the accommodation issue remained unresolved for several hours despite attempts to contact the local organisers. The initial arrangement had placed Pranati, India’s lone gymnast at the Games, and her male coach in the same room. The situation was eventually escalated to the IOA, whose intervention helped secure separate accommodation for the athlete and her coach at around 1:30 am.Pranati later confirmed the incident, telling NDTV: “Yes, there was a mix-up during the accommodation. It was resolved around 2:00 am.”Missing letter in coach’s name delays room allocationEven after alternative accommodation was arranged, Mishra faced another administrative hurdle while collecting his room keys. Hotel staff reportedly could not locate his booking in the register because the letter ‘I’ had been omitted from his name in the official system records.The clerical error had to be corrected, and his accreditation verified, resulting in a further delay of around 45 minutes. Mishra was finally able to settle into his room well past 2:00 am.Despite the late-night disruption, Pranati is fully fit and focused on her upcoming competition. The Indian gymnast’s qualification events are scheduled to begin on September 19, as she prepares to represent the country at the continental showpiece.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Definitely a shortage’: India’s Chef de Mission admits accommodation crisis at Asian Games, reveals additional rooms booked
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India’s Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav has acknowledged a shortage of accommodation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, revealing that the India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav has acknowledged a shortage of accommodation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, revealing that the Indian contingent had to book additional hotel rooms after its accommodation quota was reduced upon arrival in Japan.Yadav said the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Indian contingent had made their own arrangements for hotels and transport to ensure athletes were not affected by the logistical issues surrounding the Games.“Everyone has accommodation, and there is no problem from our side. There were some issues initially, which is why we booked an additional hotel. Our team is going directly to the airport. The accreditation process is quite lengthy and is being done on the cruise, so it is taking a lot of time. There are also some transportation issues, but we have made our own arrangements for cars and hotels for our players. We have already booked 18 rooms and will book another 10 today. There is definitely a shortage of accommodation," Yadav told reporters.The admission comes amid wider concerns over lodging, transport and accreditation in the lead-up to the official opening of the Games on Saturday.Organisers have opted against building a traditional athletes' village, instead using container-style accommodation, hotels and a docked cruise ship. The Olympic Council of Asia said Friday that all athletes and officials registered by the entry deadline had been provided Games-appropriate accommodation, while acknowledging logistical strains.‘Our priority is to look after our children’Yadav said the Indian contingent was not interested in assigning blame and would instead focus on ensuring athletes were comfortable and able to concentrate on competition.“There has been some mismanagement, but this is such a big event that anything can happen. However, we don’t want to focus on who is at fault. Our priority is to look after our children, resolve all their problems and ensure they are comfortable and well taken care of. We want them to focus on their performance, win medals and then relax. That is our wish, and that is what we are working towards," he added.Yadav also revealed that India had been informed after its arrival that its accommodation quota had been reduced, forcing the contingent to make alternative arrangements at short notice.“When we arrived here, we were informed that our accommodation quota had been reduced. So, we had to book additional hotels within a day," he said.Reports have also highlighted delays faced by several Indian athletes and teams in reaching their accommodation, while additional rooms have had to be arranged as more members of the contingent arrive.Flag ceremony delayed, then disruptedThe accommodation concerns were followed by another organisational setback on Friday when the traditional flag-hoisting ceremony involving India and four other contingents was delayed and then abruptly disrupted.The ceremony at Garden Pier, involving Yemen, North Korea, Palestine, India and Timor-Leste, began after a 20-minute delay before being halted. Organisers initially said: “We are sorry for the delay. There is some trouble with a team. We will try to restore in another 15 minutes.”The disruption eventually lasted more than an hour. Organisers later attributed it to a communication problem between the Olympic Council of Asia Executive Board and the Organising Committee.India's deputy chefs de mission A Sharath Kamal and Anjali Bhagwat had begun moving towards the dais before returning to the waiting area after the ceremony was delayed again.“I have not seen such a scene before,” Yadav told PTI.The ceremony eventually went ahead, with former shooter Bhagwat and former sprinter Lijo David Thottan representing India.The disruption added to the logistical concerns surrounding the Games, even as India prepared to enter Saturday's official opening ceremony, with double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time defending Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor named the country's flag-bearers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Este Aston Martin de Rowan Atkinson es único en el mundo y está en venta por 325.000 euros
articles.standfirst: Se trata del modelo que estuvo en el Salón de Ginebra de 1986, y el actor pidió a Aston Martin que se lo preparara para competición sin dejar de ser legal en carretera.
articles.summary: Se trata del modelo que estuvo en el Salón de Ginebra de 1986, y el actor pidió a Aston Martin que se lo preparara para competición sin dejar de ser legal en carretera.
articles.body: Más allá de la interpretación, que siempre es vocacional, el actor británico Rowan Atkinson tiene una pasión que podríamos calificar de enfermiza por los coches. Quizá ni siquiera él mismo sepa el número total de los que ha poseído, entre los cuáles ha tenido incluso un McLaren F1 cuya cotización actual ronda lo 20 millones de euros. Su pasión no es algo excéntrico entre el mundo de las estrellas, ya que en Reino Unido la pasión (y el conocimiento) por el automóvil es muy alta y son muchos los personajes populares que se han convertido en coleccionistas o casi. Por citar algunos de los más conocidos, ahí están los nombres de Eric Clapton, Jay Kay (vocalista de Jamiroquai) o Elton John. Pero el modelo que ves en estas imágenes es una rareza absoluta. Primero porque, siendo un Aston Martin V8, se trata de una versión carrozada por Zagato. Solo se construyeron 89 unidades entre 1986 y 1989, 52 con techo cerrado y 37 en versión Volante (descapotables). El coche se presentó al mundo en el Salón de Ginebra de 1986. De hecho, esta unidad que ves, la primera en ser fabricada (antes hubo dos prototipos), estuvo allí mismo exhibiéndose. Para entones había sido ya adjudicada a Rowan Atkinson, cuyas posibilidades económicas siempre fueron muy altas incluso antes de saltar a la fama. Solo que el actor no se conformó con tener el mismo coche con el que podían pasearse otras 88 personas; él quería una unidad con la que participar en carreras, pero que al mismo tiempo fuese legal para rodar por la calle. Todo aquello lo podía haber conseguido acudiendo a un preparador. Pero, en lugar de ello, habló directamente con Aston Martin para que se lo modificasen a su gusto. Pidió que subieran la potencia original de 432 CV, que finalmente se quedó en 478 CV, que le pusieran ventanillas aligeradas, una jaula antivuelco, un depósito más grande de competición, instrumentación adicional, etc, etc. No se sabe lo que al actor le costó todo ello, que está documentado con multitud de documentos y fotografías, pero debió ser una fortuna añadida a un coche que de serie ya costaba 142.500 euros al cambio, que equivaldrían hoy a 420.000 con la inflación de la vida. Se sabe que el cómico empleó en efecto el coche para correr en las carreras del Aston Martin Owners Club, en la que por supuesto solo participan modelos de la firma británica. Y no se sabe en qué momento el coche acabó arrinconado en su garaje ni en qué año lo acabó vendiendo. Lo novedoso para los aficionados de la marca en la que corre Fernando Alonso es que esta rareza vuelve a estar en el mercado. El coche tiene solo 10.000 km aproximadamente y lo vende un coleccionista particular afincado en Alemania por 325.000 euros. No es un precio de risa.

articles.title: BBC broadcasts FIA World Rally Championship from 2027
articles.summary: The BBC will broadcast the FIA World Rally Championship across the UK from 2027-29.
articles.body:
The BBC will broadcast the FIA World Rally Championship across the UK from 2027-29.

The new deal includes coverage of all 14 WRC rounds each season, with five live stages plus the power stage from each rally, 14 one-hour highlights programmes, digital clips and additional content across BBC platforms.

Rally Scotland will receive extensive live coverage across all four days of competition, giving audiences in the UK live, free-to-air access to the country's first WRC round since 2019.

Hugh Chambers, CEO of Motorsport UK, the organisation behind Rally Scotland, said: "The BBC agreement gives Rally Scotland and the wider WRC a national platform from 2027, helping us reach long-standing fans and bring new audiences into the sport."

Welshman Elfyn Evans leads the 2026 championship with one round of the season remaining, the Rally Italia Sardegna from 1 October to 4 October.

articles.title: Anu Raghavan and the pursuit of Asian Games podium she never got, despite a medal
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: New Delhi: For eight years, 400m hurdles athlete Anu Raghavan has been an Asian Games medallist without ever standing on the podium. The certificate i.
articles.body: New Delhi: For eight years, 400m hurdles athlete Anu Raghavan has been an Asian Games medallist without ever standing on the podium. The certificate is with her. The bronze medal, however, is not.When Bahrain's Kemi Adekoya was stripped of the 2018 Asian Games gold after a doping violation, Raghavan moved from fourth to bronze. On paper, history changed. In reality, nothing did. There was no medal ceremony, no flag raised in Jakarta, and no applause from a packed stadium. Just an amended result sheet and an absence that has lingered ever since."I won the bronze medal at the Asian Games despite finishing fourth," Raghavan tells TimesofIndia.com. "But even now, I am sad because I still don't have that medal in my hand. I have a certificate, but that feeling of being an Asian Games medallist is not entirely there," she continued.On September 28 in Aichi-Nagoya, the 33-year-old will finally have the opportunity to claim that moment.Indian athletics has produced its share of comeback stories, but few have unfolded with quite as many detours.Raghavan's journey began long before international medals arrived. A national champion from the U-14 age group, she graduated through the Asian and World Junior circuit before establishing herself as one of India's premier one-lap hurdlers. Her breakthrough arrived in 2017 when she won a silver medal at the Asian Championships in Bhubaneswar, clocking a then personal best of 57.22 seconds.Yet the defining chapter of her career, in rather controversial circumstances, came a year earlier.In 2016, Raghavan was omitted from India's Olympic relay squad despite being among the country's leading quarter-milers. She challenged the decision in court, and the controversy became one of the biggest selection debates in Indian athletics.Rather than ending her career, Rio became a turning point."As everyone knows, I was eliminated from the team in the first Olympics in 2016," she says. "After that, I thought that if I continued, maybe my life would be fulfilled in sports. I realised I wasn't an international medallist yet, so I had to work for it," she explained.Two years later came Jakarta. She finished fourth in 56.92 seconds — then the race of her life. Months later, the bronze arrived by revision, not celebration.Paying to keep the dream aliveWhat followed was perhaps even harder than the baggage of the Rio Olympics.Elite athletics is expensive, particularly for athletes outside cricket's financial ecosystem. After changes to Kerala's athlete support programme following the pandemic, Raghavan found herself funding her own career while continuing to compete nationally."For the last five years, I have been training outside. I was spending my own money," she says. "To compete in Indian Series meets, there is travelling, accommodation, everything. Our monthly salary is simply not enough," she explained her hardships.The Palakkad-born remained a national medallist almost every year, yet sponsorship proved elusive."I worked hard for five years to get sponsorship. After 25, it is very difficult to get one. Reliance Foundation gave me a chance. I was 32 years old, and they trusted me," she said.The timing was significant.Her mother's prolonged illness and subsequent death had left her questioning whether continuing was worth the emotional and financial burden."I was under a lot of pressure because of my mother's condition, and later her death. But they gave me confidence that I can survive in any situation," added the athlete.An event that chose herAsk most hurdlers why they chose their event and you'll hear stories about speed or rhythm. Raghavan's answer is different."The event chose me," she laughs.As a schoolgirl, she played Kho Kho before entering Kerala's sports division. Coaches tested her across sprinting, middle distance, jumps and hurdles. Her endurance stood out immediately."My coach wanted me to run 400 metres. I kept telling him I wanted hurdles. He promised that once I reached Plus One (Class 11), he would make me a 400m hurdler. That's exactly what happened."She never looked back.From Asian Juniors to World Universities, every significant international appearance came in the 400m hurdles — an event widely regarded as one of athletics' most demanding disciplines.It is neither a sprint nor a distance race. Ten hurdles interrupt rhythm every 35-45 metres, forcing athletes to combine speed, endurance and technical precision while fatigue steadily dismantles mechanics.Focus on not just trainingIf there is one theme that runs through Raghavan's 2026 season, it is sports science.Modern athletics has become obsessed with data: force plates, stride analysis, biomechanical sensors and race modelling. For Raghavan, those numbers did something years of training couldn't.They restored belief."Earlier, we were just training," she says. "Now we are using data, analysis, electronic equipment. We can actually read our strength. When I compare my numbers, I know I'm not weak. That's what gave me confidence," she said.Confidence mattered because her body had already tested her once this year.She crashed during the Federation Cup and dislocated her elbow. The injury briefly threatened her Asian Games campaign, but she recovered in time and produced the fastest performance of her career - 56.54m at the Indian Championships - this season to seal her place in India's squad.I was talking to a mindset coach because I felt I could not handle the pressure anymore. I even thought about leaving the sport. She asked me: 'Why did you start?' I kept thinking about that for an hour. After that, everything changedThe difference, she insists, wasn't physical. It was mental."I was talking to a mindset coach because I felt I couldn't handle the pressure anymore. At this age, I even thought about leaving the sport," she says. "She asked me one question: 'Why did you start?' I kept thinking about that for an hour. After that, everything changed," she said with a smile.One last surge towards the podiumWith the Asian Games on the horizon, training became surprisingly uncomplicated. There are fewer heavy strength sessions now. Less emphasis on raw speed. More repetition of one thing: execution."We're focusing on race pattern now," Raghavan explains. "Earlier it was fitness and speed. Now it's about how to execute the race in competition," she explained the process as the Asian Games begin on September 19.Execution, in the 400m hurdles, means knowing exactly how many strides separate each barrier, where to attack, where to conserve, and how to resist panic when lactic acid begins flooding the legs after hurdle six.Even her mental preparation follows the same script."I visualise the race," she says. "I think about my legs, my speed, and how I want to execute every hurdle."Eight women from Asia are faster and younger than Raghavan, and six of them will compete in Aichi-Nagoya. The women's 400m hurdles in Asia is deeper than it was in 2018.But medals are not always the only measure of redemption.For an athlete who fought Olympic exclusion, financed her own career, rebuilt herself after personal loss and waited years for recognition of a medal she had already earned, Aichi-Nagoya offers something more meaningful than another entry on her résumé.It offers the opportunity of finally hearing her name announced as an Asian Games medallist: in real time, on the track, with the podium waiting.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bayern and England’s Kane not focused on Ballon d’Or despite 73-goal season
articles.summary: Harry Kane could become first Ballon d’Or from England since 2001, but striker focused on Bayern Munich trophies.
articles.body:
Harry Kane ‌described the 2025-26 campaign as the best season ⁠of his ⁠life after scoring 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England, and while his performances have made ⁠him a leading candidate for the Ballon d’Or, he says he is not focused on individual awards.

No ⁠English player has won the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001, and Kane is up against tough competition with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in the ‌running.

“I’ve never liked talking too much about myself. The only thing I’d say is that last season was incredible, both personally and for the team,” Kane told Spanish outlet Marca in an interview published on Friday.

“It was, by far, the best season of ⁠my life.”

Kane said he was proud ⁠of his tally of 73 goals, which was the highest since Lionel Messi netted a record 82 times in 2011-12, but that it ⁠might not be enough to claim the mantle as the world’s best player.

“I’m ⁠extremely proud of that … but ⁠the Ballon d’Or isn’t in my hands. It depends on the people who vote. As far as I’m concerned, last season is in ‌the past.

“Now I’m focused on this one and I’m looking forward to seeing what else I can achieve.”

The ‌winner ‌will be announced at the official awards ceremony on October 26.

articles.title: India star Sooryavanshi urged to be patient by coach Gambhir
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi told to be patient after playing back up to Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson in Sri Lanka series.
articles.body:
India coach ‌Gautam Gambhir said Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to ⁠wait for his ⁠chance to break into the side after he left the 15-year-old prodigy on the sidelines of ⁠their three-match Twenty20 series sweep against Afghanistan.

Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson opened for India in the series, with ⁠Abhishek scoring the third-fastest century in T20 internationals in Thursday’s 127-run victory in New Delhi.

Sooryavanshi, who was the highest scorer in this year’s Indian Premier League, made his international debut against ‌England in July, but the top-order batter failed to make an impact as the hosts dominated India in the T20 series.

He scored two fifties against Zimbabwe in Harare later that month but has not played for India since.

“Whether you’re a 15-year-old or a 30-year-old, when ⁠you have to wait for your ⁠opportunity, you have to wait for your opportunity,” Gambhir told reporters after the match.

“We know the kind of talent he has and what he ⁠can do, but someone who has been performing for the last two to three ⁠years will always be ahead of ⁠someone who has just entered the team.”

Sooryavanshi will travel to Nagoya for India’s Asian Games campaign, with a one-off T20 against hosts Japan set ‌for Tuesday before the Asiad quarterfinal on September 28.

“Whenever he gets his run, he will get a longer run ‌as ‌well … We want competition and talent in the dressing room,” Gambhir added.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 opening ceremony: When and where to watch live in India
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: The Asian Games 2026 officially begin in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday, September 19, with India aiming to improve on its record medal haul from th.
articles.body: The Asian Games 2026 officially begin in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday, September 19, with India aiming to improve on its record medal haul from the previous edition in Hangzhou.The opening ceremony will feature Indian Olympic medallists Manu Bhaker and Tajinderpal Singh Toor as India’s flag-bearers. Bhaker made history at the Paris 2024 Olympics by winning two medals, while Toor enters the Games as the defending Asian champion in men’s shot put after winning gold in the last two editions.The 20th edition of the Asian Games will see athletes from 45 countries and regions compete across 43 sports. Japan is hosting the continental event for the third time, after Tokyo in 1958 and Hiroshima in 1994.India will look to better its performance at Hangzhou 2023, where it won a record 107 medals, including 28 gold. The Indian contingent includes major names such as PV Sindhu in badminton, Mirabai Chanu in weightlifting, Manu Bhaker in shooting, Aman Sehrawat in wrestling and Lovlina Borgohain in boxing.India’s athletics contingent also features more than 75 athletes, including Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar, Murali Sreeshankar, Jyothi Yarraji and Parul Chaudhary.Asian Games 2026 Opening Ceremony: When and where to watchWhen is the opening ceremony?The Asian Games 2026 opening ceremony takes place on September 19 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Time: 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM local Japan time (JST) / 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM Indian Standard Time (IST)Where can you watch the opening ceremony on TV in India?The event will be telecast live on Sony Sports 1 and Sony Sports 5. articles.title: Shiv Kapur, last to win Asian Games gold in golf for India, hopeful two-decade-long medal wait will end
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: More than two decades after winning India’s only individual Asian Games golf gold, Shiv Kapur believes the country’s current crop of golfer.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than two decades after winning India’s only individual Asian Games golf gold, Shiv Kapur believes the country’s current crop of golfers has the talent to bring another medal home from Nagoya.The golf competition at the 2026 Asian Games begins on Sept 30, with India fielding a six-member contingent comprising Yuvraj Sandhu, Veer Ahlawat and Saptak Talwar in the men’s event, and Pranavi Urs, Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok in the women’s competition.Kapur, who scripted history with his individual gold at the 2002 Busan Games, said that medal remains the defining achievement of his career and hopes the long wait finally comes to an end. “It’s been more than 20 years since my gold medal, and I’m hoping this team breaks that jinx. Even today, that medal remains the biggest achievement of my career because it belonged to India as much as it belonged to me,” Kapur, now 44, said on the sidelines of an IGPL event in Delhi.India has steadily emerged as one of Asia’s strongest golfing nations, with multiple players competing in Asia and Ladies European Tour. Kapur feels the experience within the squad, combined with the confidence gained from recent international performances, gives India a genuine chance of challenging for medals in both team and individual events.Having represented India across multiple editions of the Asian Games, Kapur said the tournament carries a unique emotional weight that is unlike any professional event. “When you’re playing for India, it’s completely different. Every shot means more because you’re representing the country, not just yourself. That’s what made Busan so special for me,” he said.The former Asian Games star also believes Indian golf is entering an encouraging phase, with a stronger domestic structure producing players capable of competing consistently at the highest level.As Nagoya approaches, Kapur hopes the next chapter of India’s Asian Games story will belong to a new generation, as he concluded, “Records are meant to be broken. I’d be happier than anyone if one of these boys or girls comes back with the gold. That’s how Indian golf moves forward."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Amid mismanagement, Typhoon alert threatens to derail Asian Games 2026 at Aichi-Nagoya
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: After facing accommodation crisis ahead of the opening ceremony, Aichi-Nagoya is now bracing for another major challenge, with a possible typhoon thre.
articles.body: After facing accommodation crisis ahead of the opening ceremony, Aichi-Nagoya is now bracing for another major challenge, with a possible typhoon threatening to disrupt the Asian Games 2026 and affect athletes and officials. The latest weather concerns come just days after torrential rain flooded parts of the city, disrupted transport and forced hundreds of athletes and officials to temporarily evacuate their accommodation.Organisers are preparing for possible weather-related disruption in the opening days of the multi-sport event, as Tropical Storm Dujuan is forecast to approach Japan’s central Pacific coast on Monday, September 21. The storm threat comes just days after torrential rain hit Nagoya and surrounding areas, forcing hundreds of athletes and officials to temporarily evacuate their accommodation and causing delays to some competitions.The Games officially open with the ceremony on Saturday 19th September, although football, basketball and volleyball events have already begun in the region.Organisers prepare for possible typhoonAs on Thursday, Tropical Storm Dujuan was located off Japan’s Pacific coast and moving northwest towards central Japan, where Nagoya is situated. It had maximum sustained winds of 90 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 126 kmph.Japan’s chef de mission for the Games and Japanese Olympic Committee executive board member Kosei Inoue said organisers were preparing for possible severe weather.“Due to the heavy rain and severe weather, some competitions have already experienced delays or postponements, and there is also a possibility that a typhoon could approach on September 21,” Inoue told Reuters.He added that the JOC was holding detailed meetings to ensure it could respond appropriately to changing conditions.Athletes could be evacuated if conditions worsenNagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa, who is also the deputy president of the Games, said the competition would continue under normal rainy conditions, but emergency measures would be introduced if severe weather posed a risk to athletes.“Under normal rainy conditions, the Games will carry on as usual,” Hirosawa told Reuters.“However, in the event of torrential rain that triggers emergency alerts, we will arrange for the athletes to evacuate temporarily.”The organisers have also prepared a contingency plan for the Costa Serena, the Italian cruise ship being used to accommodate thousands of athletes and officials. If winds reach typhoon strength, the ship will leave the dock and move offshore to safer waters.“Additionally, if we encounter typhoon-level strong winds, the cruise ship will move offshore. We already have clear protocols in place for situations like these,” Hirosawa said.Severe rain has already disrupted preparationsThe latest weather threat follows torrential rainfall in Nagoya last week, which flooded parts of the city, disrupted train services and forced schools to close. Several hundred athletes and officials were also temporarily evacuated from their accommodation.Some competitions have already experienced delays or postponements due to the severe weather, adding pressure on organisers as the event approaches its official opening.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The 15 Most Anticipated Revenge Games in Recent Sports History
articles.summary: On Saturday night, Lane Kiffin will return to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium less than a year after abruptly leaving Ole Miss for LSU amid College Football Playoff preparations.
articles.body:
On Saturday night, Lane Kiffin will return to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium less than a year after abruptly leaving Ole Miss for LSU amid College Football Playoff preparations.

The Oxford police are calling in reinforcements from neighboring states in preparation for the hostile environment awaiting one of the most anticipated revenge games in recent sports history.

But is it No. 1 on that list? Not even close.

In honor of Kiffin's return to Ole Miss, we've taken a stroll through the last quarter-century to find the 15 most anticipated revenge matchups across all sports.

The focus here was the anticipation, not necessarily the vitriol or the in-game performance. Tom Brady suiting up for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Foxborough drew as many cheers as boos, but it was undoubtedly one of the most anticipated in recent years.

Jack Eichel, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2015 NHL draft, spent six seasons with the Buffalo Sabres. He tallied 337 points in 354 games over his first five full seasons and looked like a franchise cornerstone, as evidenced by his being a team captain in each of his final three years in Buffalo.

However, the relationship between team and player soured when Eichel suffered a herniated disc in his neck in March 2021. The Sabres recommended fusion surgery, while he preferred disc replacement. When neither side budged, he was stripped of his captaincy after failing his physical and was placed on injured reserve before eventually being traded to Las Vegas.

His return to KeyBank Center drew a chorus of boos, but his postgame comments are what earned this one a spot on the list.

"It was the loudest I've heard this place ever," Eichel told reporters . "Really. It only took seven years and me leaving for them to get into the game. ... They must just [have been] booing because they wish I was still here."

Kawhi Leonard steadily climbed from being a role player on an established contender to the best player on the Spurs roster during his seven seasons in San Antonio, winning the 2014 Finals MVP and two Defensive Player of the Year awards.

However, he played only nine games during the 2017-18 season because of a mysterious right quad tendon injury. He was cleared to play by the team doctors, but his own camp disagreed and he stayed out of action, creating a fracture between Leonard and the organization.

He was shipped to the Raptors that summer in exchange for a package built around DeMar DeRozan. His return to San Antonio brought chants of "traitor!" and "quitter!" while the Raptors lost in a 125-107 blowout. The icing on the cake was DeRozan recording his first career triple-double in the game.

David Ortiz and Manny Ramirez might have been the stars of the 2004 Boston Red Sox squad that broke the Curse of the Bambino, but Johnny Damon was the face of that team and the unofficial leader of the self-proclaimed "Idiots" that endeared that franchise to the city.

When he reached free agency after the 2005 season, he publicly stated that the New York Yankees were the one team he would not sign with. He made it clear he would love a reunion with the Red Sox. However, a four-year, $52 million deal from Boston's bitter rivals was enough to change his mind.

The hero-to-villain turn was swift. Damon showed up at Fenway Park for his return in May, looking like a different person, with his signature long hair and beard trimmed to meet the Yankees' team policy.

Signs calling him "Judas Damon" littered the stands. The rivalry hop still stands as one of the biggest betrayals in Boston sports history.

All-Time Most Expensive Sports Memorabilia

Saquon Barkley burst onto the scene to win 2018 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors. The next five years brought ups and downs, including a torn ACL and some terrible Giants teams in general, but he still tallied 7,311 all-purpose yards and 47 touchdowns across his six seasons in New York.

After Barkley played the 2023 season on a franchise tag and logged 962 rushing yards in 14 games, the Giants opted to let him test the free-agent market without a standing offer. Fans got to watch his departure firsthand on HBO's Hard Knocks: Offseason .

He ended up landing with the rival Philadelphia Eagles on a three-year, $37.75 million deal, as the jersey burning was underway . Boos rained down in his return to New York. He torched the Giants for 176 yards and a touchdown on his way to a 2,005-yard rushing season and Offensive Player of the Year honors.

"It's kind of hard not to hear that," he told reporters after the game. "I think I kind of, I didn't help myself when I said earlier in the week, I didn't think I was going to get booed, but they're booing for a reason. It's a compliment at the end of the day. That's how I took it."

Alex Rodriguez spent the first seven seasons of his career in Seattle. He reached free agency for the first time coming off an age-24 season in which he logged an AL-leading 10.4 WAR.

Rodriquez's departure from the Mariners seemed likely, but the narrative shifted when his publicly declared desire to play for a contender was undermined by him signing a massive 10-year, $252 million deal with a Texas Rangers team coming off a 91-loss season.

The "Pay-Rod" moniker was born. On his return to Safeco Field, fans showered the field with boos and Monopoly money to further drive the point home.

Rodriguez slugged an AL-leading 52 home runs in his Rangers debut in 2001, while the Mariners won a franchise-record 116 games in their first year without him.

"If you guys will have me back, I plan on re-signing here." That's what Kyrie Irving told a Boston crowd at a fan event outside TD Garden on Oct. 4, 2018. But after an ugly 2018-19 season where team chemistry eroded with Irving at the center of the splintering, he signed a four-year, $141 million contract with the Brooklyn Nets.

Celtics fans didn't forget that promise. They didn't forget his sage-burning stunt in his first preseason game back in Boston in December 2020, either.

They held onto their resentment and vitriol until his first trip back to TD Garden in front of a full-sized, post-COVID crowd during the first round of the 2021 playoffs.

Constant boos and chants of "Kyrie sucks!" filled the stadium throughout Game 3. It was far from a one-off night of anger, though.

In Game 4, he intentionally stomped on the Celtics logo at mid-court. He also flipped off the crowd behind his back when the boos continued the following year.

Not surprisingly, the boos continue each time he steps onto the floor in Boston.

Ole Miss was coming off a 4-8 season and four straight years without a bowl appearance when Lane Kiffin took over as head coach after a three-year stint at Florida Atlantic. By his second year, he had built them into a 10-win team.

In 2025, he had them sitting at 11-1 and preparing for a College Football Playoff run when he shocked the college football world by packing up and accepting a massive contract from SEC rival LSU. The Rebels were left to navigate the CFP under interim coach Pete Golding, though they managed to win two games to advance to the semifinals.

With Oxford PD deploying its 150-person force alongside out-of-state mounted patrol units from Mobile and New Orleans, the environment at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday is expected to be intense. The fact that it will be No. 7 LSU vs. No. 8 Ole Miss only further fans the flames in what is expected to be one of the defining games of the 2026 season.

8. Shaquille O'Neal vs. Los Angeles Lakers

The Los Angeles Lakers built a dynasty around Shaquille O'Neal and Kobe Bryant, but the two superstars could no longer coexist during a contentious 2003-04 season that ended in a surprising loss to the Detroit Pistons in the NBA Finals.

Faced with a choice, the Lakers shipped O'Neal to the Miami Heat in exchange for Lamar Odom, Caron Butler, Brian Grant and a first-round pick. The NBA schedule-makers jumped at the opportunity to put Shaq's first return to L.A. front and center on Christmas Day.

An icy pregame greeting between Shaq and Kobe Bryant helped set the tone. The game was a thriller, with Bryant dropping 42 points as the Heat escaped with a 104-102 overtime win.

The crowd provided a mix of cheers and boos upon Shaq's return, as the page was turned on a legendary era of Lakers history.

John Tavares spent nine seasons with the Islanders, delivering on the expectations of being the No. 1 overall pick in 2009 to develop into the face of the franchise. He spent five seasons as team captain and scored 621 points in his time with the organization.

He repeatedly assured the Islanders that he wanted to stay with them, only to turn around and sign a seven-year, $77 million deal with the Toronto Maple Leafs in free agency. To make matters worse, he celebrated the signing by tweeting a picture of himself as a child sleeping under a Maple Leafs bedspread with the caption: "Not every day you can live a childhood dream."

The fans were merciless in his return to Nassau Coliseum, burning his jerseys in the parking lot, hurling plastic snakes at him during warmups and drowning out a video tribute with boos. The peak of the night came during the third period, when chants of "It's your bedtime!" and "Where's your jammies?" helped close out a 6-1 Islanders rout.

6. Terrell Owens vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Terrell Owens could do no wrong in his first season with the Eagles in 2004, hauling in 77 catches for 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns to transform the offense. He then returned from a fractured fibula to play in the Super Bowl, where he had nine receptions for 122 yards.

With the first season of his seven-year, $49 million contract in the books, T.O. then torpedoed all of that goodwill by demanding his contract be renegotiated . Public criticism of quarterback Donovan McNabb and the Philadelphia organization led head coach Andy Reid to suspend him indefinitely . The chaos reached its peak with his iconic driveway interview , where he did shirtless sit-ups for reporters.

The Eagles ended up cutting ties with Owens by releasing him in March 2006 . He twisted the knife further by signing a three-year, $25 million contract with the rival Dallas Cowboys.

When he returned to Philadelphia in October, the crowd provided exactly what you would expect from a Philly crowd. Owens was held to three catches for 45 yards while allowing an interception on a pass that deflected off his hands in a 38-24 Eagles win.

Brett Favre spent 16 seasons with the Packers before a tearful retirement following the 2007 season. But when he changed his mind a few months later and wanted to return to Green Bay, his job was no longer waiting for him. Aaron Rodgers was firmly entrenched as the new starting quarterback.

A standoff ensued, with Packers general manager Ted Thompson offering Favre a $20 million marketing contract to stay retired, but he refused and was eventually traded to the New York Jets. His late-career narrative then took an even more surprising turn when he inked a two-year, $25 million deal with the Minnesota Vikings the following offseason, joining a longtime rival.

Favre threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns in a Week 4 victory over the Packers in Minnesota, but the true revenge game moment came in Week 8 when he returned to Lambeau Field. The beloved franchise quarterback was booed relentlessly, while " Traitor 4-Ever " shirts lined the stands, but he responded with 244 yards and four touchdown passes in a 38-26 win.

4. Kevin Durant vs. Oklahoma City Thunder

A homegrown superstar who helped usher in the franchise's move from Seattle to Oklahoma City, Kevin Durant was as beloved by his city as any athlete in recent memory during his time with the Thunder.

Playing alongside Russell Westbrook, he led the Thunder to the Western Conference Finals in 2016, building a 3-1 lead against a 73-win Warriors team before suffering three heartbreaking losses in a row. Rather than running it back with a legitimate contender in OKC, he jumped ship and joined that very same Warriors team in free agency that summer, inking a two-year, $54.3 million max contract.

He was jeered as a "cupcake" by fans on his return, a nod to an Instagram post from Westbrook after Durant's departure and former teammate Kendrick Perkins' preferred term for a player he deemed soft.

The boos erupted throughout warmups and every time Durant touched the ball. Things got particularly heated when he and Westbrook yelled back and forth at one another during a third-quarter timeout.

In the end, Durant was largely unfazed. He dropped 34 points in a 130-114 Warriors victory.

"When Figo jogged across to take a corner in the 72nd minute, debris rained down. Among the coins and bottles settled a suckling pig's head, a cochinillo. The game was delayed for 12 minutes as referee Luis Medina Cantalejo and his assistants tried to restore order."

That's just a snapshot of the scene, courtesy of Sky Sports , when Luis Figo returned to Camp Nou for what was actually his second match back in front of the Barcelona fans following his surprising move to join rival Real Madrid.

His transfer stemmed from an agreement his agent had signed with Real Madrid presidential candidate Florentino Pérez, who made signing Figo a centerpiece of his campaign. Pérez was not expected to win, but when he did, backing out of the agreement would have triggered a massive financial penalty. He ultimately departed for Real Madrid with a then-record buyout clause of roughly $56 million.

The crowd noise was deafening at his first match back in 2000, but the pig's head two years later marked the climax of what still stands as one of the biggest betrayals in sports history.

After 20 seasons, six Super Bowl titles, four Super Bowl MVP awards and three league MVP awards in New England, Tom Brady hit the free-agent market in 2020 after growing tension with Patriots head coach Bill Belichick over roster construction, his contract situation and a lack of offensive weapons led to an eventual split.

Brady inked a fully guaranteed two-year, $50 million contract with the Buccaneers and immediately led them to a Super Bowl title, throwing for 4,633 yards and 40 touchdowns in his age-43 season.

The following year, he retu rned to Gillette Stadium in Week 4 on Sunday Night Football. The crowd cheered him as he took the field for warmups but booed him on Tampa Bay's opening drive. A fair divide between legacy and fandom.

To add to the highly anticipated game, Brady overtook Drew Brees as the NFL's all-time leader in passing yards midway through the game. Despite not throwing a touchdown pass, Brady came away with a 19-17 victory.

LeBron James completely reshaped Cleveland's sports landscape when the Cavaliers selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2003 NBA draft. He led them to the 2007 NBA Finals and earned two MVP awards in his first seven seasons with the team.

His first trip to free agency was one of the biggest storylines in recent sports history. He turned it into a media circus with "The Decision," which is when he announced live on ESPN that he would be "taking his talents to South Beach" and joining the Heat.

Cavaliers owner Dan Gilbert published an infamous letter in response, referring to the move as a " cowardly betrayal " and galvanizing the city against its former hero.

The venom in the stands for his return to Quicken Loans Arena was on another level. He responded by torching the Cavs for 38 points on 15-of-25 shooting over three quarters as the Heat won 118-90.

LeBron eventually returned to the Cavs in 2014 and delivered a title two years later. But immediately following his departure, there was not a more hated man in the state of Ohio.

articles.title: Predicting Sami Zayn Storylines, Feuds and When He Loses the Undisputed WWE Championship
articles.summary: After a disappointing nine-day reign, we're eager to see if Sami Zayn can persevere with new challengers nipping at his heels.
articles.body:
After a disappointing nine-day reign, we're eager to see if Sami Zayn can persevere with new challengers nipping at his heels.

"Last Real Good Guy" defied the odds for a second time, defeating CM Punk to become the new Undisputed WWE Champion. Many fans saw his first world title win at Night of Champions as a fluke or a consolation prize.

Reigns' In-Ring Legacy Is Getting a Rewrite 📝

Penta's Time as WWE Champion Is Coming 👀

Many didn't believe he would regain the company's most coveted prize so soon. Nevertheless, Punk's ambition to be a fighting champion backfired as Zayn capitalized on a chaotic finish during their rematch in Mexico City.

With Money in the Bank three weeks away, the 42-year-old has a massive chip on his shoulder and an even bigger target on his back. Let's try to predict how the Canadian star's latest tenure as world champion will pan out.

SmackDown's world title picture is more interesting than it has been in months. Unfortunately, Zayn has made a lot of enemies on the brand since he turned heel.

Obviously, Punk and Cody Rhodes will eventually seek a rematch. Johnny Gargano is also expecting him to honor their deal and give him the first shot at his newly acquired championship gold.

Expect Zayn to renege on his promise, setting Gargano up as a potential Money in the Bank participant. Gunther and Finn Balor will also be in the mix when WWE announces the qualifying matches for SmackDown.

Although Bron Breakker is the early favorite, Kevin Owens would be an exciting pick to win the men's ladder match. Instead, we're betting Owens and Punk will challenge Zayn in a triple-threat match at the upcoming event.

Initially, many suspected Zayn vs. Punk would be the blockbuster main event for WWE/AAA/NXT Worlds Collide. However, the crossover show reportedly isn't scheduled to stream live on Sept. 26, and the match isn't advertised on Allstate Arena's website .

Money in the Bank is the likely destination, and a triple-threat match makes the most sense considering the build. Despite the odds, Punk and Owens' lingering animosity will likely give the champ a chance to survive until the next premium live event.

A Showdown With Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel

Zayn is a great fit as the current champion because it's too soon to revisit Punk vs. Roman Reigns. It would also be a shrewd move to leverage the reaction to this win at Night of Champions ahead of WWE's return to Saudi Arabia.

According to Mike Johnson of PWInsider , multiple sources stated that Zayn regained the world title because WWE wants him to headline Crown Jewel with Reigns in November.

That would line up because the two didn't interact during his first reign. The men's and women's Crown Jewel Championship matches have also become an annual tradition, and this is an ideal matchup.

Riyadh will give Zayn a warm welcome, creating an atmosphere similar to their 2023 encounter at Elimination Chamber. Conversely, it will extend his reign and provide a marquee match where his title isn't at stake.

It's a safe bet that Reigns will win and move on to this year's men's WarGames match a few weeks later. Meanwhile, his former stablemate will have his head on a swivel for the rest of 2026.

Sami Zayn Will Drop The Title On SmackDown

Television title changes have been a mainstay under the current creative regime. So, expect Zayn to drop the title in the weeks leading up to or after Survivor Series.

The PLE takes place on Nov. 28, three weeks after Crown Jewel and two weeks before Wrestlepalooza. WWE's final "Big Four" event of the year routinely has a five-match card to compensate for the men's and women's WarGames matches.

More importantly, the event hasn't held a traditional WWE championship match since 2019. That could change this year, but it's easier to assume Zayn won't defend his title at Daikin Park in Houston, Texas.

It's a bit harder to predict who will defeat him. Owens is long overdue for another world title run, but Punk currently seems like the most logical choice. Considering how he lost to Zayn, it doesn't seem like the company is done with him as champion.

articles.title: Ranking WWE and AEW's Biggest Breakout Stars of 2026
articles.summary: WWE and AEW have had their fair share of fresh faces break out in a major way in 2026 and ascend to new levels of stardom.
articles.body:
WWE and AEW have had their fair share of fresh faces break out in a major way in 2026 and ascend to new levels of stardom.

Both companies were in desperate need of new blood on their respective rosters coming into the new year. All in all, they've done an exceptional job of bringing in and calling up several stars who have been difference makers.

Chad Gable and Penta are currently the hottest they've ever been, but both began to break out in 2025, leading to the success they've had with the Intercontinental Championship in 2026. The same can be said for Jacob Fatu and Kyle Fletcher, who were already on the cusp of main event greatness last year.

Although Ricky Saints, Blake Monroe, Joe Hendry, Steven Borden and Zayda Steel have also arrived in recent months, they're all in the process of finding their footing and have yet to hit their stride.

These are WWE and AEW's biggest breakout stars of 2026.

At the onset of 2026, Powerhouse Hobbs was one-third of the AEW World Trios champions. Within weeks, he was gone from AEW and an entrant in WWE's Royal Rumble match. Rechristened as Royce Keys, he went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal and has since cemented his spot toward the top of the card as the leader of the new 946 faction.

Fed up with being relegated to midcard and tag team purgatory in WWE, Tommaso Ciampa allowed his contract to expire and immediately jumped ship to AEW at the end of January. Even as a seasoned veteran, he had one of his best years ever in 2026 by capturing the AEW TNT Championship, competing on several pay-per-views, feuding with Chris Jericho, challenging for the AEW World Championship and so much more. This was the Tommaso Ciampa fans had long waited to see.

Ethan Page wrapped up his super successful stint in NXT in April to make way for his move to the main roster. He's been an entertaining fixture in the Intercontinental Championship picture this entire time and has racked up impressive wins over Rey Mysterio, Je'Von Evans and Penta. That Intercontinental title is undoubtedly in his future.

AEW signing Persephone to a dual contact while she simultaneously wrestles for CMLL was a genius move. She was originally a regular in Ring of Honor before building momentum in AEW, winning the CMLL World Women's Championship and unseating Maya World at All In for the AEW TBS Championship. She's become a major force in that women's division in a relatively brief period of time.

Fatal Influence wasted no time in making an impact in their debut on the post-WrestleMania SmackDown. All three members have been standouts so far, but Jacy Jane in particular has excelled. In addition to it not being hard for her to generate genuine heat from crowds, she bested Tiffany Stratton for the Women's United States Championship, her first of what should be many titles in WWE.

Maya World getting signed to AEW largely stemmed from her and Hyan stepping up in the absence of Nixon Newell and Miranda Alize to face TayJay in a tag team match last October on Collision. They were booked for many matches after that, and their commitment to the craft along with the skills they showed earned them a full-time contract with the company.

Even after they put pen to paper with the promotion, they were still utilized as an enhancement team and were exclusive to Ring of Honor. World's impressive outings over there led to her getting booked for AEW more and more, and when Sareee had to be pulled from the 2026 women's Owen Hart Cup, World was yet again right there to seize the opportunity.

World went way further in the bracket than anyone could have expected. Her win over Athena sent her to the finals with Mercedes Moné at Double or Nothing, where she narrowly fell short following a phenomenal performance.

AEW wisely had her capitalize on that momentum by having her win the AEW TBS Championship at July's Redemption pay-per-view. Her reign was unfortunately cut short by Persephone at All In, but there's no question that she's proven her worth as championship material and will hold gold again eventually.

It wasn't long into Je'Von Evans' NXT tenure that it was clear he'd be one to watch for years to come.

It'd be almost impossible for fans not to have their eyes permanently peeled for Evans with the way he gracefully flies through the air anytime he's in action. He's also incredibly likable to boot, so it was always going to be a big deal once he inevitably landed on the main roster.

Evans joined the Raw roster at the very end of 2025 and had standout showings in the Royal Rumble match, inside the Elimination Chamber and in the Intercontinental Championship Ladder match at WrestleMania 42. He remained in the hunt for the Intercontinental title in the months that followed and ripped it up with the likes of Ethan Page, Rusev and Penta.

His feud with Big Cass kept him occupied for a brief bit coming out of SummerSlam, but now his sights are firmly set on the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match and walking away with that opportunistic briefcase. The chances of actually winning are low, but he'll shine as only he can.

At only 22-years-old, he has his entire career ahead of him.

Reigns' In-Ring Legacy Is Getting a Rewrite 📝

Penta's Time as WWE Champion Is Coming 👀

Sol Ruca is very similar to Je'Von Evans in the sense that she's a human highlight reel and made a name for herself in NXT with her awe-inspiring athleticism and natural charm.

Ruca spent much longer in NXT but also had more success, having won the WWE Women's Speed Championship and the NXT Women's North American Championship. She never got the chance to win the NXT Women's Championship, but that's because she was due to be called up to Raw after WrestleMania 42.

Her inexperience was apparent from the get-go, but she gradually worked through the nerves and won the Women's Intercontinental Championship from Becky Lynch by Clash in Italy. The reign itself was forgettable, but she did have two quality title defenses against Lyra Valkyria and Raquel Rodriguez.

Rodriguez would end Ruca's reign in their rematch, but Ruca has remained a constant on Monday nights as part of her program with The Judgment Day. She has been exactly what the women's division needed, and as she continues to put the pieces together, she'll become a big star.

It's difficult to label Andrade El Idolo a breakout star when he's had multiple stints in WWE and AEW along with several other promotions, but the heights he's reached this year were at one point believed to be unfathomable by some.

Andrade could have very easily been doomed to stepping stone status, but once he returned to AEW early on in 2026, he was determined to become the top talent many hoped he would be years ago. Sure enough, he came across as more motivated than ever before and had some stellar matchups with Swerve Strickland, Kenny Omega and Adam Page.

His alliance with The Don Callis Family may have been brief, but it did spawn his current rivalry with MJF. It also led to him beating Mark Davis for the AEW National Championship at Redemption and earning a future shot at the AEW World Championship by winning the Casino Gauntlet match at All In.

There is a very real possibility of Andrade becoming the top title holder in AEW very soon, and until then, he's being positioned as one of the biggest babyfaces in the company. That's quite the turnaround from being one-half of a random tag team with Rey Fenix on SmackDown around this time a year ago.

Kevin Knight was already trending in the right direction during his time in the tag team division last year with Mike Bailey, but breaking away from Bailey was really put him on the path toward main event glory.

Following a quick run with the AEW World Trios Championship alongside Adam Page and Bailey, he clinched the vacant AEW TNT Championship at Dynasty and went on to defend it more times than anyone else in the history of that title.

He had a handful of excellent title defenses against the returning Brian Cage, Bailey, Darby Allin and even MJF.

He took his singles career to the next level by betraying Allin at the end of Double or Nothing, severing ties with Bailey on the subsequent Dynamite, and becoming the newest member of The Don Callis Family. All of that got him a pay-per-view main event with Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship, which he obviously lost but benefited from big time.

Knight is no longer TNT champ following his Falls Count Anywhere loss to Allin at All In, but AEW seems to be building him up as a future world champion and rightfully so.

Trick Williams spent so long in NXT and accomplished almost everything he possibly could on the brand (including invading TNA and holding their world title hostage) to the point where it was comical just how overdue he was for a main roster call-up.

He hit SmackDown on the first Friday night of 2026 and instantly had an aura about him. Strong showings at Royal Rumble and Elimination Chamber boosted his stock and resulted in him walking out of WrestleMania 42 the new United States champion.

The matches he had during his first reign were nothing to write home about, but the promos and crowd work were wildly entertaining. His alliance with Lil Yatchy also got over massively and became a weekly fixture on the blue brand.

There's still room for improvement as far as Williams' in-ring ability is concerned, but he checks every other box and is nearly the complete package of what WWE wants out of their world champions. He'll be in that spot at some point, but no time soon.

He's had a terrific year and there's no need to rush him into something he's not ready for.

Thekla first made her toxic presence felt in AEW last summer, but it wasn't until 2026 that she truly got going and became the focal point of the women's division.

Toni Storm taking time off after Revolution opened a huge void in the AEW Women's World Championship picture, one that Thekla didn't hesitate to take. Although she was initially unsuccessful in unseating Kris Statlander as champ, she stole the gold in their rematch and defeated her for a third time at Revolution.

From The Brawling Birds to Thunder Rosa, a slew of stars stepped up but were put down by Thekla. She became undeniable in the ring but also on the mic, electrifying audiences whenever she was given time to talk.

She has a legitimate vibe about her that no one else in the women's division does. The cadence of her promos combined with the swag in her step make her must-see television, which is why it was disappointing that she dropped the AEW Women's World title before she could make it to Wembley Stadium for All In.

The Toxic Spider has since rebounded and will be fighting Willow Nightingale at All Out for an opportunity to reenter championship contention. Regardless of the result, she's still one of the most over stars on the roster.

Oba Femi went from never having appeared on either Raw or SmackDown (outside of a cameo in the crowd) to being one of the hottest commodities on WWE's main roster in the span of one month.

WWE portraying him as the face of the future during Saturday Night's Main Event last December sent the message that he had to be taken seriously as soon as he showed up as a permanent member of the main roster. That's why he lasted for so long in the men's Royal Rumble before answering Brock Lesnar's open challenge for WrestleMania 42.

The build to the bout was masterful and the match played out practically perfectly with Femi decisively destroying Lesnar in one of the year's greatest triumphs. It was very much a passing-of-the-torch type of moment, even though they continued to feud on and off through SummerSlam where Femi beat him inside Hell in a Cell.

Realistically, Femi should have already won the World Heavyweight Championship by now, but all signs point to WWE wanting to wait until WrestleMania 42 in Saudi Arabia to give him his crowning moment. It's not often you see a Superstar have as hot of a rookie year as he has, a testament to just how spectacular of a start he's gotten off to and the high hopes officials have for him going forward.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: NHL Power Rankings for Every Team Ahead of the Start of the 2026 Preseason
articles.summary: T-minus one day.
articles.body:
Pucks drop around the NHL with seven preseason games on Saturday and shots and passes begin for real on Sept. 29 when the 2026-27 regular season gets started with games in Raleigh, N.C., Toronto, Boston, Edmonton and Las Vegas.

It's all got the B/R hockey staff on the brink of rapture but collective sanity was harnessed long enough to open with a set of Power Rankings looking at each of the 32 teams on preseason eve.

Not surprisingly, nothing could be finer than to be in Carolina to start the season, as the reigning Cup champs copped the No. 1 position, followed by last season's President's Trophy winner, an Eastern Conference finalist, and a team not so far removed from scheduling two straight raucous celebratory parades.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | Utah Mammoth | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The Canucks weren't very good last year. And they won't be very good this year either. Even if Manny Malhotra were to wave a wand and bring his highly-drafted son, Caleb, to the NHL right away, even having a third overall pick wouldn't do much good. Can Elias Pettersson ever resemble a player earning $11.6 million a season?

OK, full marks to the Calgary brass. It may be a bit before the Flames are legitimately relevant again. But they've done a good job accelerating a rebuild that's seen them move some people while watching others leave. This is a team that won 50 games and a Pacific title and amassed 111 points as recently as 2021-22, a roster from which only forward Mikael Backlund remains.

Quick, name a Seattle player you'd move heaven and earth to get onto your team. Yeah, us neither. Matty Beniers and Shane Wright are solid NHL'ers but have only occasionally looked like second and fourth overall picks, mostly Beniers. If they'd have gotten Jason Robertson to agree to come over from Dallas, who knows? But they didn't.

Slowly but surely, Kyle Davidson is getting it done. He drew the magic ticket and picked Connor Bedard first overall in 2023, added future goalie Spencer Knight in a trade with Florida and added suddenly well-traveled defenseman Bowen Byram in a trade with Buffalo. Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar are good young forwards and even Patrick Kane is back for a chance to be an elder example.

There are some who'll suggest the sky isn't falling in Winnipeg, even in the absence of Connor Hellebuyck, because much of what's left over was good enough to snag a President's Trophy in 2024-25. We'll soon see how much of that successful regular season was Hellebuyck's doing and what Josh Morrissey and Mark Scheifele can do without him.

OK, so everything's all better, eh? Zach Werenski won a Norris Trophy amid constant speculation that he wouldn't stay long term, but he vetoed a trade to Dallas in late June and arrives to this season suggesting "Columbus is where I want to play, where I want to win, and where I want to be for a long time." He'll be eligible to extend with the Blue Jackets on July 1, 2027.

Chalk the lack of confidence in the Red Wings up to the bad optics of their captain, Dylan Larkin, asking out. It doesn't help that they've not made the playoffs in ages, a drought that finally cost GM and franchise icon Steve Yzerman his job. Still, the cupboard isn't entirely empty with the likes of Moritz Seider and Lucas Raymond still in the fold.

No offense to the fine hockey fans in the Midwest, but it's difficult to get super excited about a team that's not only missed three of the last four playoff tournaments but also unloaded one of its best in Jordan Kyrou. But all of a sudden there's a lot of young talent in St. Louis that shouldn't be slept on. Don't believe us? Ask an Edmonton fan if they'd like Dylan Holloway and Philip Broberg back.

Certainly there are fans in Nashville who will shriek, "stop talking about the 2024 offseason already!" And they have a point. But the Predators haven't done anything significant enough in the last two years to make anyone forget what now looks like an ill-fated big free agency swing. Is there veteran talent? Yes. But enough to win anything? No.

This just in: Matthew Schaefer is a stud. And goalie Ilya Sorokin is a legit NHL elite as well. Exactly what the Islanders get from guys not wearing sweater numbers 48 and 30, though, will determine how close they get to the front-running Hurricanes and the rest of the Metropolitan Division. Last year, they were four points out of fourth place and eight points south of the playoff cut line.

It's easy to dismiss the Rangers based on last season's disaster but it's easy to look at a roster with Igor Shesterkin, Adam Fox, Mika Zibanejad, and now Pavel Dorofeyev and think things can be better after all. The holdovers aren't young, but Dorofeyev, 25, injects youth and a goal-scoring pedigree after netting 72 goals across what became his final two seasons with Vegas.

Welcome to the big time, Gavin McKenna. The Penn State alum goes from the serenity of Happy Valley to the hockey madness of Toronto as an 18-year-old. No pressure, eh kid? If he comes in on the level of a Macklin Celebrini or Connor Bedard, the Maple Leafs will happily add him to a group that already includes Auston Matthews and William Nylander. And now Sergei Bobrovsky, too.

Out with franchise icon Anze Kopitar. In, for a full season, with supernova forward Artemi Panarin. But is what's left around him enough to make noise in the Pacific and the West as a whole? Maybe not. Having four of your top-six defensemen, and six of your top eight, past their 30th birthdays might not be an ideal setup.

The good news? Sidney Crosby is clearly Pittsburgh's best player. The bad news? Sidney Crosby is clearly Pittsburgh's best player. And perhaps the next two in line, Evgeni Malkin and Erik Karlsson, are each closer to 50 years old than 20. So while they'll be good enough to keep people in the seats until No. 87 goes, it won't be ring-worthy.

The biggest name transaction of the offseason didn't exactly go in Ottawa's direction, did it? It was one thing to know Brady Tkachuk wasn't enthralled with the idea of being in Canada's capital, it was another to actually see the move to Florida occur. Can the likes of Tim Stutzle and Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot move it forward, especially in light of Chabot's annoyance at his ex-teammate?

It's easy to see the variance in opinions on the Devils. Some see them as a playoff team and a genuine contender in the Metropolitan. Others expect them to be in the out-of-the-playoffs tier for the third time in four years. Jack Hughes is a flat-out force when he's healthy, but the second part isn't always reliable. And hey, if they can get big brother Quinn into the fold, watch out.

Whether an offer-sheeted Leo Carlsson would have made a significant difference is up for debate, particularly in a debate-friendly place like Philadelphia. But here's some reality, if your two leading scorers are tied for 55th (Travis Konecny) and 57th (Travor Zegras) in the league, there's some ground to cover before scheduling a parade.

Good enough to be respectable or maybe slightly better? Sure. Good enough to win a stacked Atlantic Division and truly compete for the city's first Cup since 2011? Probably not. But hey, a team could do a lot worse than throwing David Pastrnak and Charlie McAvoy out there for 20-plus minutes each night. What they get beyond that will largely determine where they wind up.

Will the Sharks be this year's Ducks? Anaheim only finished six points ahead of San Jose last season but it turned out to the difference between missing the playoffs and reaching (like the Ducks did) the second round. Macklin Celebrini arrived as a 100-point player and is a legit superstar but it'll take more than just him to get the franchise over the relevance threshhold.

The Ducks probably arrived a bit earlier than expected and ended Edmonton's Western dynasty while doing so, and they've locked up Leo Carlsson and Cutter Gauthier for the long term, too. But their defense took a hit with the offseason exits of John Carlson, Jacob Trouba and Radko Gudas.

It's hard to argue with the star power of Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard, but there's some aging underneath, questions about goaltending, and who knows what it's all going to look like when the Mike Babcock Era officially begins on Sept. 29. They could win a Cup or they could be looking for a new coach by the holiday season and shopping McDavid at the deadline.

There are several teams in the league who, if they were stocks, would send investors into a buying frenzy. The Mammoth are one of them. They've got a horde of young players who've proven themselves NHL-ready and they acquired a hot prospect goalie in Sebastian Cossa in the offseason. If he lives up to the hype, it's the beginning of prolonged relevance in Utah.

It wasn't easy to find optimism about the Sabres heading into last year, and losing Alex Tuch wasn't a great look, but they're young and they're skilled and they're loaded. Defenseman Rasmus Dahlin played like a No. 1 overall pick (2018) last season he was ranked fourth in the league at the position by NHL Network.

Having the league's all-time leading goal scorer is going to guarantee a steady relevance, but it seems to be warranted. They've consistently gotten value from other teams' castoffs and brought in the likes of Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou this offseason to bolster the ranks around Alex Ovechkin. Can Logan Thompson continue to be one of the NHL's best goalies? Stay tuned.

Luring Quinn Hughes to Minnesota made the Wild a contender and keeping him in town will continue that run. Kirill Karizov and Matt Boldy are certainly worthwhile pieces, too, but they haven't shown an ability to get the team out of the Central Division.

How much was real and how much was John Tortorella? That's the question in Vegas, where the Golden Knights scuffled to "just" 95 points and fired Bruce Cassidy on the way to winning the Pacific (just five points up on the conference's eighth-seeded playoff team), then won 14 playoff games. Welcome to the NHL, new coach Ryan Craig.

Depth has been the selling point in Dallas for years and it's no surprise given the presence of Mikko Rantanen, Miro Heiskanen and the recently signed Jason Robertson for at least one more year. If Jake Oettinger holds up his end, the Stars will be in the mix.

That the Lightning have remained relevant since their last Stanley Cup hoist in 2021 is testament to the competitive muscle memories of Nikita Kucherov and Andrei Vasilevskiy, among others. But they're in a difficult Atlantic mix with Buffalo and Montreal and have been bounced from the first round of the playoffs in four straight seasons. When the relevance ends, it might be abrupt.

Go ahead, you tell the Panthers that one year out of the playoffs negates the idea that they're a real contender after parades in 2024 and 2025. They're hardly a team full of youngsters, but adding Brady Tkachuk from Ottawa does boost the nastiness quotient and getting Alexsander Barkov back from injury is a huge plus. C'mon, would anyone really be shocked if they won again?

It's a good time to be a hockey fan in Montreal. Nick Suzuki and Lane Hutson are studs, Cole Caufield is excellent, and Jakub Dobes showed signs of being "the man" in goal in the playoffs. He won nine games, and had a 2.66 goals-against average and a .908 save percentage in the Canadiens' run to the Eastern final.

The Avs rolled to 55 wins, 121 points and a President's Trophy last season and it got them into the Western final for the first time since they won it all in 2022, but it didn't mean much when they encountered Vegas last spring. Still, having Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar isn't a bad thing. Can MacKenzie Blackwood and Scott Wedgewood win it all? We'll see.

It's pretty great to walk into training camp as the defending champions and that's what the Hurricanes get to do that one else does. That they've managed to put together a Cup-winning team with better than $8 million in cap space remaining is impressive.
