articles.title: Asian Games: India's Quimcy Dsouza reaches Teqball semis, one win away from historic medal; mixed doubles pair eyes bronze
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza moved within one win of creating history after reaching the women's singles semifinals in teqball at the Asian Games in .
articles.body: India's Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza moved within one win of creating history after reaching the women's singles semifinals in teqball at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Friday.Making her Asian Games debut, Quimcy upset top seed Yuina Sakamoto of Japan 2-1 (10-12, 12-11, 13-11) in her first Group A match.She followed that up with a 2-0 (12-9, 12-7) win over Cambodia's Koemyean DY in her second group match, finishing on top of Group A and booking a place in the semifinals.By topping the group, Quimcy received a bye in the quarterfinals.The 24-year-old will face Indonesia's Sumaya in Saturday's semifinal. A win will guarantee India its first-ever medal in Teqball, one of the six sports making its Asian Games debut.Even if she loses in the semifinals, Quimcy will still have a chance to win bronze on Sunday.Mixed doubles pair eyes bronzeIn the mixed doubles event, Quimcy and Mohammed Anas Imran Beg were beaten 0-2 (7-12, 10-12) by Vietnam's Hoang Minh Tan Nguyen and Gia Nghi Trinh in the quarterfinals.However, the Indian pair remain in contention for a bronze medal after winning their repechage match.Quimcy and Beg began their campaign with a 2-0 (12-10, 12-3) win over the Philippines pair of Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Augustin in Group A before losing their next match 1-2 (8-12, 12-7, 10-12).They then suffered back-to-back defeats, losing 0-2 (3-12, 8-12) to Cambodia's Thuonvireak Bun and Sophornraksmey Yorn, and by the same score to Thailand's Phakpong Dejaroen and Suphawadi Wongkhamchan.The Indian duo bounced back with a 2-0 (12-1, 12-6) win over Salman Alebraheem and Hessah Alfailakawi to reach the quarterfinals, where they lost to Vietnam.In the repechage round, Quimcy and Beg defeated Abulencia and Augustin for the second time on the same day, winning 2-0 (12-3, 12-6) to stay in the race for a medal.Teqball is one of six sports making its Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya, alongside Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), Padel, Surfing, BMX Freestyle and Virtual Taekwondo.The sport combines elements of football and table tennis. It was invented in Hungary in 2014 by Gabor Borsanyi, Gyorgy Gattyan and Viktor Huszar, while the first official Teqball World Championships were held in Budapest in 2017.In Teqball, players use every part of the body except their hands and arms to rally a standard size-five football across a curved table divided by a transparent plexiglass net.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ryan Clark again accuses ESPN of leaking his firing to OutKick: Here’s the real story
articles.summary: Ryan Clark accused ESPN of leaking his firing news to OutKick on "The Breakfast Club," but a detailed behind-the-scenes timeline challenges him.
articles.body: Ryan Clark once again accused ESPN of leaking the news of his firing to OutKick to embarrass him. This time, he said so during an appearance on the influential Black radio show "The Breakfast Club." "Everybody that got laid off got told on Tuesday. Only one person got told on Monday on set. Me. That’s the distinction," Clark told the hosts Tuesday. "It was also purposeful. It was also meant, in my opinion, to humiliate. In leaking it to OutKick, you now know if anybody is going to curry favor for you in this decision, it’s going to be them because it’s me." ESPN informed Clark of his firing during a commercial break of the July 22 edition of "NFL Live." He did not return to the program. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He continued, "There’s so many reputable sports publications. Whether it’s you know Sports Illustrated, the New York Times, The Athletic. If this is going to be as big a news as it turned out to be, why not give it to them? Because you knew who you were giving it to. You knew the small amount of people within that building that knew it. Then the humiliation that you at least purposed it to come along with me being laid off." "I do feel like it was about that humiliation, and he wanted to save me from that. It was already going to be enough written. It was already going to be enough laughs, enough jokes that I worked that day anyway. So I appreciated him." This is not the first time Clark has made that claim. Nor is it the first time listeners of "The Breakfast Club" have heard it. The day after OutKick reported the news, one of the show’s hosts claimed a source told them ESPN executive Burke Magnus leaked the information to OutKick to spite Clark. It is possible the source was someone who spoke with Clark — or Clark himself. The version of events Clark and the show’s hosts are presenting, however, is not accurate. I would know. I am one of three people who know how OutKick obtained the information and why ESPN informed Clark of his firing during a live program. So let’s go step by step. TOMI LAHREN DEFENDS OUTKICK'S ESPN SCOOP, TORCHES JEMELE HILL, BACKS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM We must first return to Super Bowl week in February. Although the game aired on NBC, agents, executives, and on-air talent from various networks routinely descend on the host city for meetings and negotiations. One of the most notable pieces of information to emerge that week was that Clark’s standing at ESPN had deteriorated ahead of the network’s first Super Bowl broadcast in 2027. Sources told us Clark was unlikely to remain part of ESPN’s "Monday Night Countdown," which was scheduled to serve as the network’s Super Bowl pregame and halftime show. They also questioned whether he would remain with ESPN at all. The rumblings were not entirely surprising. Despite what Clark says, he was not universally loved inside ESPN. He had supporters, including Stephen A. Smith, ESPN NFL studio executive Seth Markman, and Mina Kimes. But he also had plenty of detractors. Complaints about Clark included his handling of previous contract negotiations, including videos and regular updates; demeaning comments about Robert Griffin III for marrying a white woman; an on-air and behind-the-scenes blowup with Peter Schrager; reckless comments about Louisiana police; and multiple headlines that had little to do with sports. ESPN would not fire Clark over any single incident. The network tends to tread carefully when dismissing Black talent because of the risk of false accusations of racism, accusations Clark eventually made anyway. Waiting for a broader layoff period made sense. Those rumblings continued throughout the spring and summer, especially after ESPN omitted Clark from its upcoming Super Bowl plans during the network’s May upfront presentation. Before July, OutKick also reported several times that Clark’s future with ESPN was uncertain. RYAN CLARK MADE IT TOO DIFFICULT FOR ESPN TO JUSTIFY KEEPING HIM AFTER YEARS OF CONTROVERSY Now let’s jump to July. On Friday, July 17, a friendly media ally told me they had heard ESPN planned to let go of Clark the following week, when the network was expected to announce layoffs. For context, this person was not a source. Everything we discuss is private and off the record. They did not give me the information for publication, and I had no plans to report it. Two days later, on Monday, others in the industry began asking whether I had heard about the layoffs, who was on the list, and whether Clark was among those who'd be dismissed. That afternoon, I learned that my OutKick colleague Dan Zaksheske had also heard that ESPN planned to lay off Clark on Tuesday. Zaksheske and I then gathered the information and confirmed it with two additional sources. We typically avoid reporting transactional media news, but Clark had become a significant figure in the broader sports conversation because of his racial and political commentary. We decided the story was substantial enough to report. Around 4 p.m. ET that day, in accordance with our standard editorial policy, we informed ESPN’s public-relations department that we planned to report Clark’s firing. ESPN PR said it would get back to us. Around 4:48 p.m., the network responded that it had no comment. We published our story, only to learn that The Athletic had reported a bare-bones version at approximately the same time. We later learned that ESPN informed Clark of his firing during the commercial break, right around 4:48 p.m. — before sending us its response. The timeline makes clear that ESPN did not work with OutKick. No one high up at the company leaked the information to us or intended, as Clark put it, to "humiliate" him. So why did ESPN handle it this way? ESPN has told multiple people who inquired about the situation that management did not think OutKick would hold the news until after "NFL Live." The network feared Clark would learn about his firing from our report. The executive who informed Clark — and told him OutKick knew about it — was Seth Markman, one of Clark’s allies. It appears Markman made that decision because he believed Clark was better off hearing the news directly from him. In our view, Markman handled the situation poorly and helped create the secondary storyline surrounding Clark’s firing: the OutKick angle. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE ESPN also deserves blame for assuming OutKick would not hold the story until it addressed the layoff with Clark. The fact that we reached out to the network indicated that we would wait. The network then added to the circus by tipping off The Athletic that we had the story. As for why Clark’s firing was announced a day before the rest of the layoffs, the answer is simple: He was the only person whose name moved the needle. Cam Newton was the second-biggest name laid off. OutKick reported his termination the following morning. For all the drama, headlines, and accusations, OutKick did not contribute to the situation beyond reporting the news. We heard about a story from sources and reported it after seeking comment from ESPN. Every other subplot was the product of ESPN’s poor handling of the situation and Clark accusing us of conspiring with his former bosses. To avoid another situation like this, ESPN should stop assuming our intentions are poor and do a better job keeping sensitive information concealed. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Perhaps unbeknownst to ESPN management and Clark, his impending firing was relatively well known in and around ESPN. People talk. And OutKick has never needed an intentional leak to learn what is happening inside ESPN.

articles.title: El piragüismo y el remo de Brisbane 2032 se disputarán en un río donde viven cocodrilos
articles.standfirst: Pese a la polémica, el Comité Organizador ha aprobado que el río Fitzroy, donde habitan cocodrilos de agua salda, albergue las pruebas de estas dos disciplinas
articles.summary: Pese a la polémica, el Comité Organizador ha aprobado que el río Fitzroy, donde habitan cocodrilos de agua salda, albergue las pruebas de estas dos disciplinas
articles.body: Ya es oficial. Pese a la controversia y las dudas de los últimos meses, el río Fitzroy, ubicado en Rockhampton, albergará las competiciones de remo y piragüismo de los Juegos Olímpicos de Brisbane 2032, después de que el Comité Organizador haya aprobado de forma oficial la elección de este polémico emplazamiento. La presencia de cocodrilos de agua salada y la propensión de esta cuenca hidrográfica, la segunda más grande de Australia, a las inundaciones y fuertes corrientes -que podrían generar condiciones desiguales en la competición- pusieron en el punto de mira este río, ubicado a 600 kilómetros de Brisbane. Sin embargo, y pese a que se recogieron miles de firmas para que estas competiciones se trasladaran de lugar, la Federación internacional de remo encargó una evaluación independiente "exhaustiva y rigurosa" en la que se han basado para adoptar la decisión. "Ahora sabemos que el río Fitzroy es capaz de proporcionar condiciones de competición justas durante los Juegos", declaró Jean-Christophe Rolland, presidente de la Federación Internacional de remo. En la evaluación, no se abordó el tema de los cocodrilos. Pese a todo, los organizadores garantizaron que se implementarían distintos procedimientos y medidas en caso de avistar alguno de estos reptiles. En años anteriores, se localizaron ejemplares de gran tamaño, incluido uno de 4,6 metros capturado en 2023. Ahora se estima que pueden vivir en torno a 500 cocodrilos.

articles.title: Red Sox Provide Pair of Injury Updates Following Win Over Rangers
articles.summary: Here's the latest on Contreras and Chapman following Thursday's win.
articles.body:
The Red Sox secured a thrilling 4-3 win on Thursday night to avoid the sweep against the Rangers, but two key injuries stood out amid the celebration.

Star first baseman Willson Contreras left the game right before Trevor Story 's game-winning home run, and star closer Aroldis Chapman was not available when Boston tried to protect a one-run lead in the ninth. Both players are crucial to Boston's chances at making a deep playoff run, and with less than two weeks until the playoffs begin, the team needs to be smart with injury management.

After the win, the Red Sox gave injury updates on each player, and they were both encouraging compared to how serious the injuries could have been. The Red Sox head to Tampa Bay to play the surging Rays next, where they will continue to manage these injuries with the playoffs in mind.

Here's the latest on Contreras and Chapman following Thursday's win.

Contreras had to leave Thursday night's game after getting hit by a pitch in his hand, but the injury does not appear too serious. The first baseman said that even though it felt like he fractured his hand, the x-rays came back negative.

"Sore. Painful. My hand was numb for like five minutes," Contreras said, via Chris Cotillo . "That was the reason I came out of the game. I have fractured, before, the same hand. It felt like a fracture. Thankfully, it's not a fracture on the top of the bone. I'm just frustrated."

It's still too early to tell whether Contreras will be in the lineup for Friday night's series opener against the Rays, but the Boston should feel relieved that Contreras doesn't have a broken bone in his hand.

When the Red Sox took a one-run lead into the ninth inning, Boston surprisingly went to Garrett Whitlock to close it out instead of Aroldis Chapman. After the game, Chad Tracy revealed that Chapman is dealing with an injury to his lat that the team is monitoring.

"He's just dealing with some lat tightness we're going to be conservative with," Tracy said, via Cotillo . "It's getting better, but we've got to make sure it gets there. That's why he wasn't available tonight."

Whitlock worked around a single and induced a game-ending double play to secure the save, showing that he can step in at closer when Chapman is unavailable. Chapman has not pitched since Sunday and has only appeared in two games since Labor Day for the Red Sox.

articles.title: Alejandro Tosti's caddie quits midway through first round in Asheville
articles.summary: Cliff Ellis, who has looped for Tosti on and off in recent years, had enough, excusing himself from Tosti’s bag during their ninth hole of the day.
articles.body:
Alejandro Tosti's caddie quit midway through Thursday's first round of the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship in Asheville, North Carolina.

First reported by Golfweek , Cliff Ellis, who has looped for Tosti on and off in recent years, had enough, excusing himself from Tosti's bag during their ninth hole of the day.

Tosti, who was grouped with Luke Clanton and Spencer Oxendine, was even par at the time and went on to card a 1-over 72.

Reached by Golfweek via text, Tosti wrote, "He couldn't keep up with eight pars in a row," followed by several laughing emojis.

Tosti, the 30-year-old fiery Argentine, has a long history of squabbles with fellow competitors, staff and caddies, including Ellis. He was suspended from the Korn Ferry Tour in 2023 for conduct unbecoming a professional. Tosti has also been open about his mental struggles, telling Golfweek two years ago, "It's been the challenge for me my whole life, dealing with myself."

He tees off Friday at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove at 1:49 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo named in Portugal’s Nations League squad despite retirement hint
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo hinted last month that he has entered the final year of his football career
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in Portugal 's squad by new coach Jorge Jesus ahead of their upcoming Nations League fixtures.

The 41-year-old indicated that this summer's World Cup was his final one, and he dropped a fresh retirement hint last month when speaking to Vogue as he admitted: "This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy."

He will turn 43 ahead of the 2028 European Championship, the next major tournament on the calendar.

Friday's squad announcement represents the first selection by Jesus, who took charge following the departure of Spaniard Roberto Martinez after Portugal's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup round of 16. Jesus previously managed Ronaldo at Saudi side Al-Nassr, winning the league title together last season.

Addressing Ronaldo's position in the side, Jesus noted "all the called-up players are at my disposal."

"If he performs well, he plays. If he doesn't perform well, he doesn't play. That's how I treat everyone," Jesus said, before adding a caveat.

"Now, does Cris have a different status? Yes. His career is different," he said. "He has five Ballon d'Or awards. But does that influence my decisions? No. It doesn't influence anything, zero, but he is different from the others."

The 72-year-old manager has also led a number of Portuguese clubs during his career, including Benfica and Sporting Lisbon.

Ronaldo stands as the highest-scoring player in men's international football history with 146 goals, with his crowning achievement coming when he helped Portugal win Euro 2016.

He is currently targeting 1,000 career goals, standing on 979. Asked whether he expected Ronaldo to achieve that landmark for his country, Jesus appeared sceptical.

"I think he's more likely to score his thousandth goal for Al-Nassr than for the Portuguese national team," Jesus said.

Portugal begin their Nations League schedule at home to Wales on 24 September. They visit Norway three days later and play in Denmark on 1 October, before hosting Norway on 4 October.

articles.title: Rome Odunze shares Bears HC Ben Johnson's vision for the offense
articles.summary: Chicago Bears receiver Rome Odunze says head coach Ben Johnson's vision is focused on "individual execution" regardless of the score.
articles.body:
It was well-known what Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson wanted to do this season -- he wanted to be the highest-scoring offense in NFL history.

After scoring 59 points in the season opener against the Carolina Panthers , Chicago seems well on their way to doing just that. However, according to receiver Rome Odunze , Johnson is still making sure the offense pays attention to the little details so they can continue to improve each and every week.

"The head of the snake in Ben Johnson says he wants be the most prolific offense in history," Odunze said. "So, it takes those attention to details even when you score 59 points, harping on those things that you can improve on to get to that point. So, we're all bought into that and we're all trying to accomplish that. So, regardless of the points on the board, it's about our individual execution every single play."

Photos from Bears' historic 59-37 win over Panthers in Week 1

Odunze's play of the game came on a 47-yard grab where he completely mossed Carolina defender Will Lee III , which ultimately set up a one-yard touchdown run from running back D'Andre Swift to give the Bears a 14-7 lead in the first quarter. However, he only caught the ball one other time the entire game.

No one could have expected Kalif Raymond to be the leading receiver with eight receptions for 84 yards. This further supports Ben Johnson's vision because opposing defenses cannot shut down one or two playmakers for Chicago. Every skill player on the field is a threat to score a touchdown.

Chicago's next game against the Minnesota Vikings will be a bigger test for this offense. Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is not known for giving up a lot of points to opposing offenses and they shut the Green Bay Packers down in the fourth quarter of their season opener.

The most points the Bears have scored against Minnesota in the 129 times they have played each other is 52 points back in 1961; it is the only time Chicago has scored at least 50 points against the Vikings. If the Bears offense play like they did against Carolina in this game, that record could be broken this coming Sunday.

articles.title: It’s now or never for Kevin Durant in Houston
articles.summary: The Rockets are putting a lot of faith into one man.
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets had high expectations to begin last NBA season following the acquisition of Kevin Durant , until their starting point guard, Fred VanVleet , went down. That raised many questions concerning the team's functionality without a skilled guard. They still managed to win over 50 games and finish as the fifth seed in the West.

This offseason, more teams in the Western Conference have emerged as legitimate contenders, adding to an already large pool. Durant enters his second season with the team, and one that holds a lot of significance. With questions arising about team chemistry and the West growing stronger, this might be the last chance KD has to win a ring in Houston.

Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant during game two of the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at against the Los Angeles Lakers . Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images

Kevin Durant has been a premier talent in the league since he was drafted in 2007. The 16-time All-Star has won multiple championships and even brought home the MVP in 2015. Though he's entering his 19th season in the league, that hasn't changed with the Houston Rockets.

He was the main catalyst for the offense last season. Whether it was ball-handling or scoring, he was their guy. That proved to be an issue toward the end of the season when teams figured out that the Rockets lacked good ball-handlers outside of Durant. They can address this weakness with VanVleet returning, but how much better does he really make Houston?

A fifth seed in the Western Conference may be the ceiling for Houston. The Thunder, Spurs , Lakers and Nuggets all finished ahead of the Rockets last season, and that won't change any time soon. With the Trail Blazers and Timberwolves drastically improving their rosters, those might be two teams Houston finishes behind, leaving the Rockets with a tough decision to make in Year 2 of their Kevin Durant experiment.

Mar 8, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) looks up in the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images

Kevin Durant's longest stint with a team, outside of the Thunder, was four seasons with the Nets . He's played with two other teams, spending 2.5 seasons with the Suns and three seasons with the Warriors . Durant has never been the player to overstay his welcome with a franchise. It shouldn't be any different with the Rockets.

During the All-Star break, the Rockets endured a huge scandal centered around Durant. Teams usually face scandals with their younger players, not their superstar. Durant was caught using a burner account again. This time, he was speaking poorly about his current teammates and their skills on the basketball court.

It was not a good look for a player who was supposed to bring veteran leadership to the team. When the camera panned to him at the All-Star Game, Durant looked anxious and guilty. As the season progressed, it looked as though he made up with those players, but that leaves a bad taste in the mouths of everyone who's a part of the franchise.

articles.title: What To Watch For: SMU Mustangs
articles.summary: JEFF BROHM NEEDS TO GET ISAAC BROWN IN SPACE Through two games, Isaac Brown has not been able to break a big run, and he has been bottled up on a good number...
articles.body:
JEFF BROHM NEEDS TO GET ISAAC BROWN IN SPACE

Through two games, Isaac Brown has not been able to break a big run, and he has been bottled up on a good number of his rushing attempts. Both teams keyed on him when he was in the game and committed players to the box when he is in the game, and they are playing downhill, looking to stop him before he gets going. It's the right thing to do if you're a defense facing Louisville, but it has led to the rest of the offense having tons of room to operate.

There are a lot of theories about Brown's lack of production, but he did have a few runs against Villanova where he got into the second and third levels of the defense. His biggest run came right before halftime with Nova playing soft to protect against a big passing play. Brown found a cutback lane and ended up with a 26-yard run.

With teams keying on Brown, Jeff Brohm needs to scheme him into space. Brown has only had one designed passing play called for him this year. He has also not been used on jet sweeps, and he hasn't been featured as much on the option runs we've seen.

Brohm has said that they need to find ways to get Brown in space, but this week will be the opportunity to show it. SMU likes to play aggressively to create negative plays. Brown should see some screens as well as some misdirection runs to get him on the edge of the defense. Using him as a decoy has been great for the offense, but they can do both.

WILL MARK IVEY USE A SPY ON KEVIN JENNINGS

Kevin Jennings is where the SMU starts and ends. They are a team with plenty of talent on offense, but this team would struggle without Jennings. They would also be less than effective if you could contain his legs. Jennings is a great runner, but where he is at his best is when he is extending plays to find an opening.

Louisville has been aggressive so far this season with blitzes and other types of pressure looks. I think it might be in their best interest to use that fifth rusher to spy Jennings. The Cards have had very little success getting home with their pressures or with their base four-man rush. But Jennings would likely shred the defense even if they do get pressure.

Jennings finished last year completing 70% of his passes against pressure with an NFL passer rating of 101. He thrives when you come after him, and he has that option to run the ball if you don't get home. With the rush not getting home so far this year, you might be better off covering in the back end and hoping those pass rushers can get there, with Jennings having to hold onto the ball.

LINCOLN KIENHOLZ NEEDS CAN'T TAKE A STEP BACK

The first half of the Ole Miss game had some very rough moments for Lincoln Kienholz. That was the last time he looked rough. Linc has been a revelation for the offense as he has been able to beat defenses with his arm and his legs. Jeff Brohm has done a great job of utilizing him on designed runs, and Kienholz has also done well scrambling and extending plays.

The Cards can't have Linc take a step back from the way he has been playing. Louisville has a top-10 offense right now, and he is leading one of the most explosive attacks in the country. But he is the leader of what we are seeing, and there is so much more left to unlock with this offense.

No one has benefited more from defenses keying on Isaac Brown than Linc. Teams are selling out on the play-action boot plays that led to Jaleel Skinner's long touchdown last weekend. Teams are also flowing with the fake on jet sweep and sweep fakes, which has opened up massive running lanes for Linc in the middle of the field. He has to avoid making mistakes on Saturday or turning the ball over. A nice clean game from him has been what this offense needed. That can't change.

LOUISVILLE'S SECONDARY CAN EASE THE DOUBTS

The Cards have allowed three passes of 60+ yards so far this year. They've only allowed two other passes to go for 30-40 yards. The first number is the worst in the nation. The second stat would put them among the best in the country without the other big plays. But that's not how this works.

The secondary for Louisville has been questioned by many, and the numbers show why. Those three long plays account for half of the touchdowns the defense has given up this year. Two of those plays you chalk up to Trinidad Chambliss and Deuce Alexander being very good. The issue is that they've had issues in coverage on more than just the one long touchdown given up to Villanova.

The Wildcats had a wide-open receiver run free on a bad pass early in the game Saturday. They also had a 22-yard pass to another open receiver due to a coverage bust. Getting beaten by other good players is one thing. They have struggled to be on the same page in the back end, which will lead to easy points against this passing attack. They have to clean up the errors and contain the other team so that they can get the ball back to the offense to continue to do the damage they've been doing.

SMU WILL TRY TO SCREEN LOUISVILLE TO DEATH

UofL struggled to get off the field on defense early against Villanova. The reason for that was the lack of an ability to stop Nova's screen game. The Wildcats ran what I call an "abbreviated tunnel screen," where the receiver comes inside for the ball but only to get behind the tackle and guard who are sprinting out to get in front of them. They ran this over and over again to take advantage of the Cards' aggressive pass rush, and it worked. The Cards ended up adjusting, and the defensive line looked to sniff out the play during their rush.

Part of the reason that I wonder if Mark Ivey will use a spy is because I also wonder if he will look to deploy an overall scheme to contain this offense. The SMU offense can beat you over the top, but they are really at their best when Jennings is creating things with his pocket movement and his ability to get outside the pocket. Keeping everything in front of you is a sound game plan, and it also helps to make sure you don't allow the SMU quick game to turn short passes into long passes.

articles.body:
The Honeoye Falls-Lima Cougars know they are far from world-beaters after opening the season with a 41-20 loss.

"We've got guys who are going to fight (keep playing to win), but we still have a lot of undisciplined football to clean up," HF-L coach John Russ said after the Cougars earned their first win of the season in Week 2.

The Cougars erased a 14-point deficit to beat Eastridge 20-14.

HF-L opened the 2026 season at home, but against Canandaigua and minus at least two starters because of injury. As a team at one of the smallest schools in the Monroe County league, the HF-L Cougars are walking uphill this fall.

Eastridge and Canandaigua are two of five Section V Class A opponents on HF-L's schedule this season. HF-L is in the Class B group, along with 2025 state champion Monroe and 2025 Section V Class A2 champion East High/World of Inquiry.

"We have to play the big dogs," Russ said with a smile at Eastridge. He later added: "We're kind of used to playing with our backs against the wall."

While getting that first win leaves the HF-L Cougars short of world-beater status, it helps. Ask HF-L quarterback Benny Feinberg , a junior who threw a touchdown pass and had two touchdown runs in the team's win at Eastridge.

articles.title: Robinson on Gray sacking, 'manager's dream' Molloy & Dons revival
articles.summary: Stephen Robinson has been speaking to the media before Aberdeen's trip to face managerless Hibs on Saturday (15:00 BST).  Robinson says that while Aberdeen's...
articles.body:
Stephen Robinson has been speaking to the media before Aberdeen's trip to face managerless Hibs on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Robinson says that while Aberdeen's clinical finishing "carries the headlines" from their 4-0 midweek win at Motherwell, the "hard work and organisation is the big thing to take away from it".

The Dons boss has the "utmost respect" for David Gray, who was sacked by Hibs on Wednesday, and says he did a "fantastic job" at Easter Road with third and fifth-place finishes.

Robinson adds: "It just shows you how ruthless the game is now. We're six games in and he's in a semi-final so I have nothing but admiration for David as a player for Hibs and a manager for Hibs."

Robinson doesn't expect Hibs to be "that much different" under interim boss John Potter - "they haven't changed players" - and wants the "exact same form and attitude" from Aberdeen's past two games as they seek a third straight win.

On what has changed amid Aberdeen's mini revival, Robinson says: "Results. Results change everything. Results change the narrative. Sometimes you don't play as well as the results suggest, but if you win, it hides all faults. If you lose, every fault is opened up for scrutiny."

Gavin Molloy, who made just his second league start of the season at Fir Park and scored the opener, is praised by Robinson as a "manager's dream".

"Gav has had to be patient but I thought he was super," says the Pittodrie head coach. "He reminds me of Marcus Fraser at St Mirren. They just get on with it, they don't complain about anything. You can play them in any position. If they're not in the team, they train harder. He's going to get a lot of stick after me calling him a manager's dream now from the players, but he's just an ultimate pro and he got his just rewards on Tuesday night, so I'm delighted for him."

The Dons have "real high hopes" for 20-year-old Findlay Marshall, who made his first league start in midweek and "gives us legs and energy, which we don't particularly have in midfield".

Lewis Mayo and Stuart Armstrong are doubts for the game at Easter Road. Emmanuel Gyamfi will play in the KDM Cup next week and fellow long-term injury absentee Kristers Tobers is set to begin full training, which is a "real milestone for him".

Robinson has met with new chief executive Adrian Bevington, saying: "We had a really good chat. Adrian comes with a really good reputation and obviously worked at really good levels, so I'm looking forward to working with him."

articles.summary: Sean McVay may never want to go to Australia again and more NFL type news on a Friday!

If teleportation existed, and or had the Los Angeles Rams won in Australia, then perhaps Sean McVay would feel different, but as it stands McVay is happy the game in Australia is over. McVay is hopeful the Rams never have to play a game like that again.

McVay, a true company man, says the atmosphere down under was "great", however one can assume the travel, the idea of playing so far from home, the fact that L.A. got whooped up on, McVay appears content to leave that game and experience in the past.

It's interesting, and maybe one day we'll hear McVay talk about what went right and what went wrong during the team's preparation for their Australian game. As it stands, what we know is the Rams lost, and now they want to turn the page. Easier said than done.

From the sound of it, Week 1 isn't exactly all in the past, yet. In fact, Week 1 is still very much in the present, until the Rams can give fans a reason to believe otherwise. If winning is a cure-all, then losing is a deadly poison. The Rams are 0-2 in their last two games played. Facts. Can they find a cure Monday night?

"It's almost like you try and do the 'Men in Black' thing," McVay said, referencing the movie franchise, "where you say all right, 'hey I don't remember what happened.' That was so long ago. We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere. That will get taken out of context."

"Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team. What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today."

articles.title: Ronaldo named in Jesus' first Portugal squad
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, ending speculation the 41-year-old could retire from international football.

Ronaldo refused to confirm whether he would continue to play for his country after Portugal's World Cup round-of-16 defeat by eventual winners Spain in July.

But the Al-Nassr forward is part of a 25-man group chosen for Portugal's four Nations League games between 24 September and 4 October.

Jesus has replaced Roberto Martinez, who stepped down as Portugal coach after their World Cup exit.

The 72-year-old was Ronaldo's club boss last season, when the pair helped Al-Nassr win the Saudi Pro League for the first time in seven years.

The former Manchester United Real Madrid forward, who announced that this summer's World Cup would be his last, was in tears after Portugal's World Cup exit.

When asked if he would keep playing for his country, he said: "I will meet the family and take decisions with a calm head."

This sparked speculation he could follow his great rival Lionel Messi and retire from international football.

Ronaldo will turn 42 before next summer's Nations League finals and will be 43 by Euro 2028.

The oldest player in the history of the Euros is Ronaldo's former Portugal team-mate Pepe, who was 41 and 130 days for his last game at Euro 2024.

Manchester United pair Diogo Dalot and Bruno Fernandes are also in the squad, along with Ruben Dias ( Manchester City ) and Pedro Neto ( Chelsea ).

Portugal are at home to Wales on 24 September (19:45 BST) and away to Norway three days later. They then play in Denmark on 1 October and return home to host Norway on 4 October.

articles.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick jumps through table at Bills home opener
articles.summary: If Pat McAfee might be the wildest and craziest guy in all of sports television, Ryan Fitzpatrick may be a close second. The first official Thursday Night Fo...
articles.body:
If Pat McAfee might be the wildest and craziest guy in all of sports television, Ryan Fitzpatrick may be a close second.

The first official Thursday Night Football game of the season saw the Amazon Prime Video crew travel to the opening of Highmark Stadium as the Buffalo Bills hosted the Detroit Lions . The Bills got out to an incredible 21-0 start with the crowd at a fever pitch, and ended up cruising to a 41-31 victory.

Along with the opening of a new stadium comes plenty of ceremonies and festivities. But only in Buffalo will it come with a WWE-style breaking of tables. That's where Fitzpatrick comes in.

Although Ryan Fitzpatrick played in 17 NFL seasons for nine different teams, he is probably most associated with the Buffalo Bills thanks to his four seasons as a starter from 2009-2012. So it was only appropriate that he did the deed of taking an honorary table bump in the stadium to get the crowd hyped up.

You have to give Fitz credit, that was some pretty sensational form on the elbow drop. And the slow-motion replay made it look even better. If McAfee is serious about never returning to pro wrestling , maybe the former quarterback can take his place in the "former NFL player turned television analyst turned wrestler" category. Just as long as he doesn't suddenly start managing Randy Orton , we'll be good.

Speaking of the pro wrestling antics, Fitzpatrick wasn't done there. In the postgame show, he opened up his suit to reveal his glorious chest hair to an adoring crowd of Bills fans.

Ryan Fitzpatrick is definitely not your average Harvard graduate.

articles.title: Ravens vs. Saints: 5 bold predictions for Baltimore's home opener
articles.summary: The Ravens opened the season with a convincing win, and they;ll do even more convincing in Sunday's home opener vs. Saints.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens spent much of the offseason talking about standards, urgency, and creating a different attitude about execution . Now comes the first opportunity in M&T Bank Stadium this season to prove those weren't just offseason talking points.

A year ago, Baltimore struggled to establish the type of home-field advantage fans have come to expect. Several players have already acknowledged that reality this week, and Jesse Minter has made it clear that protecting home turf is a priority. Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints offers an opportunity to start changing the narrative.

That doesn't mean New Orleans should be overlooked. The Saints have explosive playmakers , a quarterback willing to challenge defenses downfield, and enough offensive firepower to create problems if Baltimore isn't sharp. The Ravens may be favored, but they'll still need to earn this one. With that in mind, here are five bold predictions for Baltimore's home opener.

Lamar Jackson accounts for four touchdowns.

Baltimore's offense looked explosive in Week 1 despite leaving some plays on the field because of penalties and a few stalled drives. The Saints just allowed more than 400 passing yards against the Detroit Lions , so here's where the rubber meets the road.

Lamar Jackson appears comfortable in Declan Doyle's offense and is already in the MVP discussion . Whether it comes through the air or on the ground, expect Jackson to be directly responsible for four touchdowns as Baltimore continues building momentum.

Rashod Bateman leads the Ravens in receiving.

Rashod Bateman finished Week 1 without an official catch after a penalty nullified his lone reception, but both he and Lamar Jackson made it clear nobody inside the building is concerned. With Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve and Zay Flowers working through a hamstring injury , Bateman should see increased opportunities. This feels like the week he reminds everyone why Baltimore continues believing in him.

The Ravens force at least three turnovers

Tyler Shough is talented. He also plays with the confidence of a quarterback willing to challenge tight windows. That mindset helped him throw for more than 400 yards in Week 1, but it also led to two interceptions and a lost fumble.

Baltimore's secondary is opportunistic, and Jesse Minter's defense creates confusion from multiple angles. The Ravens should have opportunities to take the football away.

Trey Hendrickson and Zion Young both record their first sacks as Ravens

The pressure was there against the Indianapolis Colts even if the sack totals didn't fully reflect it. Hendrickson came close on multiple occasions and consistently affected the pocket.

Eventually, those near misses become actual production. Against a Saints offensive line that will likely be forced into obvious passing situations at some point, this feels like the week Trey Hendrickson and Zion Young both get on the board.

Baltimore wins comfortably and starts 2-0

The Saints deserve respect after nearly erasing a large deficit against Detroit, but this matchup feels favorable for Baltimore. The Ravens are at home. The defense should create pressure. The offense has already demonstrated its explosiveness.

New Orleans has talented players, particularly Chris Olave , but Baltimore appears to have advantages in several key areas. Bold predictions are supposed to be risky, but none of these require Baltimore to be something it isn't. The Ravens already showed signs of being an explosive offense and aggressive defense in Week 1. This week, they put it all together—prediction : Ravens 31, Saints 20.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Iowa women's basketball's Big Ten schedule
articles.summary: Here are three takeaways after Iowa women's basketball unveiled its 2026-27 Big Ten schedule.
articles.body:
Iowa women's basketball revealed its 2026-27 Big Ten schedule on Wednesday evening, completing its full schedule in the process.

As is always the case, the Hawkeyes ' Big Ten slate is loaded with good teams and a series of challenges. What stands out from Iowa's 2026-27 slate, though?

Without further ado, here are three takeaways from Iowa's Big Ten conference schedule:

Iowa opens vs. Nebraska , travels to Michigan State on New Year's Day

Iowa opens Big Ten play with a rivalry matchup against Nebraska at Carver-Hawkeye Arena, which will obviously be a huge way to kick off the conference slate. This is especially true considering the Hawkeyes will welcome Iowa State into Carver for the annual Iowa Corn Cy-Hawk Series matchup just four days later.

As the New Year rings in, the Hawkeyes will visit Breslin Center in East Lansing, Mich., for a New Year's Day clash with the Spartans. Iowa has not faced Michigan State on the road since Dec. 15, 2024, when the Spartans prevailed over the Hawkeyes, 68-66.

How does Iowa handle its West Coast road swing

As Iowa did during the 2024-25 campaign, the Hawkeyes will travel to the Pacific Northwest to play Oregon and Washington on Jan. 24 and Jan. 27, respectively. It's always a challenge attempting to navigate the lengthy travel and time change.

"Anytime you go west, it's challenging because it's out of the normal routine," Iowa head women's basketball coach Jan Jensen said. "We did the Oregon - Washington swing two years ago and the Los Angeles swing last year, so now we know what to expect. I've made some notes on what I'd like to try differently so we can be as refreshed as possible and be as successful as we can while we're out there."

This West Coast trip also comes at the midpoint of their conference schedule, so it could set the tone positively or negatively heading into the back end of the Big Ten slate.

Iowa hosts USC, UCLA in Carver back-to-back

In what will arguably be one of the most impactful three-game stretches of the regular season, the Hawkeyes travel to Ann Arbor to face Michigan before hosting JuJu Watkins and USC and the defending national champion UCLA Bruins.

Those dates against USC and UCLA on Feb. 11 and Feb. 14 are contests every Hawkeye fan will have circled on their calendars.

articles.title: FRIENDLY FIRE: Strom Thurmond, Lincoln County coaches share competitive fire, mutual respect
articles.summary: JOHNSTON, S.C. (WJBF) — There’s been no shortage of pre-game chatter and chirping between the Lincoln County and Strom Thurmond football fanbases. And, ahead...
articles.body:
JOHNSTON, S.C. (WJBF) — There's been no shortage of pre-game chatter and chirping between the Lincoln County and Strom Thurmond football fanbases. And, ahead of Friday's marquee matchup of two of the CSRA's most storied programs, it makes sense.

Both schools are shrouded in championship pedigree with both playing for state titles last year. Strom Thurmond captured the SCHSL Class AA state crown last season while Lincoln County finished its 2025 campaign coming up just short of a GHSA Class A title against Bowdon.

The 2025 momentum has spilled over into 2026 as both squads enter Friday's game in the Peach Fields ranked No. 1 in their respective classifications.

Throw in last year's 45-20 Lincoln County victory in Lincolnton last year, and you've got every ingredient needed for elite pre-game trash talking.

But two people who won't be contributing to the bulletin board material will be the coaches. Lincoln County's Lee Chomskis and Strom Thurmond's Andrew Webb almost were almost gushing over each other as well as their respective programs and school communities.

And it wasn't just coachspeak. There's a true and genuine respect and relationship between the two programs to the point where coach Webb got the chance to speak to Chomskis' Red Devil bunch last year before making the trip to Atlanta to play for it all.

"I got to speak for their state championship week devotion and for their victory meal last year," Webb said. "To be able to go share Jesus with them. To celebrate with them coming off a seminfinal win leading into a state championship game, it was special, and I was really, really honored that Coach asked me to do that."

What makes the head coach comfortable enough to go pour into a local rival coach's program, even while still basking in his own?

"The respect that I have for coach Chomskis and his program is second to none," Webb said. "And I think the world of him and his program. I can't say enough about how much I care about him and how highly I think of his program. He does such a good job. It's such an honor to be able to compete against him and the Lincoln County Red Devils."

And, in case you're wondering, the feeling is mutual on the other side.

"[Strom Thurmond] is an incredible program," Chomskis said. "Coach Webb does an incredible job. Their staff is made up of super folks. Their kids play very hard. Very disciplined program that's had a lot of success, and they're coming off a state championship."

Both teams come into Friday's game battle tested. As impressive as Strom Thurmond has been offensively, the Rebels' defense as been especially stout.

Thurmond has won its first three contests by a combined score of 113-13, doing it against the likes of North Augusta, Abbeville and Batesburg-Leesville — none of which will be mistaken as "doormat" programs.

Meanwhile, Lincoln County's (3-1) lone loss came during Week 2 of the season in a 48-41 shootout setback to a solid Westside squad.

Last Friday, in front of a Game Night Live viewing audience, the Red Devils dispatched Harlem 35-21, though it was a costly loss as several of Lincoln County's star players went down with injury, including last week's McDonald's Players of the Game, Aiden Jones and Travis Franklin.

Jonathan Norman, who's been getting regular Division I and Power 4 recruiting attention, has already been hobbled by an ankle injury.

Meanwhile, coach Webb calls his bunch "pretty healthy" ahead of Friday's game, citing the typical "dinks and donks you're always gonna have throughout the course of a season."

Junior Kaden Wigfall has been a standout for the Rebels with five rushing touchdowns through three games, but fellow junior Zy Rouse isn't far behind with four rushing scores while averaging 6.4 yards per carry.

For Lincoln County, if Jones, Franklin and Norman can't go, or are limited, Chomskis will likely look to senior Kameron Crew, junior Sims Antonakos and Bryson Elam to tote the rock in their run-oriented scheme.

That trio performed well in relief of Lincoln County's stars last week against Harlem. But coach Chomskis is aware of what the challenge he may be up against if forced to face Strom Thurmond with limited offensive weaponry.

"I'm sure in the CSRA, people will pay attention to [this game]," Chomskis said. "It'll mean a lot to the people in Strom Thurmond and here in Lincolnton. But, you know, at the end of the day, it's just gonna be a non-region ball game. But it's going to be an opportunity to play somebody that plays good football, and hopefully we'll be able to at least stay on the field with them."

As for Webb, he's seen enough of Lincoln County to know it will pose a formidable challenge no matter who trots out on the field come kickoff time Friday night.

"We know we've gotta stop the run," Webb said. "They do such a good job of running the football. When you cut their film on, it's like watching football played in the 1980s. They run to the line. They get off the ball with low hats. They play really physical and really fast. It's really fun to watch, but it's tough to prepare for."

Both coaches have prepared their teams well for what each says should be a raucous high school football atmosphere. And Webb is prepared to set aside his fandom of Chomskis and company, at least for one night.

"I feel like [Chomskis] knows I geneuinely pull for him and just the amount of respect I have his program," Webb said. "And outside of this week, I pull for them every other week."

Under new coach Ali Jaques, Campbell will also continue to compete. Returning sophomore Jasmine Felton was named to the CAA All-Rookie Team while returning senior Jessica Woods provides stability and depth to the backcourt.

Louisiana Tech has always been the powerhouse of this conference, steamrolling to a staggering 17-1 record in conference play last season but left for the Sun Belt. Middle Tennessee is a team that will compete, as CUSA Freshman of the Year Blair Baugus is a massive return for the Blue Raiders. Historic Missouri State can potentially be an early favorite, as returner Kaemyn Bekemeier led the team in points with 17.2 and rebounds with 8.2. Lainie Douglas is another key returner, averaging 13.6 points and 6.3 rebounds per game. FIU will also compete, but losing Rhema Collins to Texas Tech is a big loss.

Green Bay is the defending conference and tournament champion after going 17-3 in conference play last season. Youngstown State finished two games behind Green Bay, finishing with a 15-5 conference play record and losing in the conference championship. Danielle Cameron provides solid shooting. Sara Baker has a strong frontcourt presence. Erica King will lock down the frontcourt, and Paulina Hernandez has size and versatility inside. All these pieces make the Penguins a strong contender. Robert Morris can also be a contender after going 11-9 in conference play last season. Mackenzie Blackford is a big transfer for Robert Morris after averaging 10.6 points at Duquesne last season. Similarly, Marshall transfer Timberlynn Yeast was named to the WNIT All-Tournament Team last season. "Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons has agreed on a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Sacramento Kings , his agents Max Wiepking, Sean Tribe and Ryan Arney tell me and Marc J Spears. The one-time All-NBA star is back in the NBA for a 10th season after sitting out 2025-26," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

Simmons took last season off to work on his mental capacity and fully escape from basketball. Now, he is back, hoping to revive his career. The former first overall pick also had interest from other teams.

"The Kings weren't the only team considering Simmons, as league sources say the Knicks and Warriors were also in the mix," The Athletic's Sam Amick wrote.

Sacramento won that battle for Simmons, but they might not be done in free agency. Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes believes the Kings will sign former first-round draft pick Cam Whitmore .

"Cam Whitmore may be on the way out of the league, but any team with a talent deficit and little to lose should be willing to give him one more shot. The Sacramento Kings fit that description pretty well, and they should have interest in seeing if there's something valuable still hiding inside the athletic wing who was recently waived by the Cleveland Cavaliers ," Hughes wrote.

The Kings are not expected to be good; however, they are putting together a roster with some intriguing pieces. Whitmore would have a lot of opportunity in Sacramento that he isn't going to have with a lot of other teams.

Whitmore was on a $15 million contract before being released by the Cleveland Cavaliers . He is a scorer, but his defense needs some work. With his career on the line, this could potentially be his last chance.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Dates, venues, sports and a growing accommodation crisis
articles.summary: More than 11,000 athletes from 45 countries will compete at world’s second-largest multisport event.
articles.body:
The 2026 Asian Games return to Japan this September bigger than ever, with several sports making their debut at the 20th milestone edition.

More than 11,000 athletes from 45 countries will compete at the world’s second-largest multisport event.

Japan will play host for the third time, following Tokyo 1958 and Hiroshima 1994, which saw their biggest medal haul of 218 medals.

Here’s everything to know about the quadrennial continental event:

When and where are the games taking place?

Officially known as Aichi-Nagoya 2026, the games will be held in Japan’s Aichi Prefecture and city of Nagoya from September 19 until October 4, although the football and basketball competitions have already begun.

The record-breaking programme will be held across 54 competition venues, including some like the Tokyo Aquatics Centre and Equestrian Park used for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

What sports are being played, and which make their debut?

A total of 43 sports will be played across 71 disciplines and 469 events.

Six sports make their Asian Games debut: surfing, freestyle BMX, mixed martial arts, padel, teqball, and virtual taekwondo.

The full list features: artistic swimming, archery, athletics, badminton, baseball, basketball, 3×3 basketball, boxing, breaking, canoe slalom, canoe sprint, cricket, cycling (road), cycling (track), mountain bike, BMX racing, BMX freestyle, diving, equestrian, esport, fencing, football, golf, gymnastics (artistic), gymnastics (rhythmic), gymnastics (trampoline), handball, hockey, judo, ju-jitsu, kabaddi, karate, kurash, mixed martial arts, pentathlon, padel, rowing, rugby sevens, sailing, sepak takraw, shooting, skateboarding, softball, surfing, squash, swimming, sport climbing, table tennis, taekwondo, tennis, soft tennis, triathlon, volleyball, beach volleyball, water polo, weightlifting, wrestling, wushu.

The opening ceremony will take place at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya from 6pm local time (09:00 GMT).

The torch relay was inaugurated in Nagoya on August 22 by three-time Olympic wrestling gold medallist Saori Yoshida and it will light the cauldron at the opening ceremony on September 19 after visiting 40 municipalities in Nagoya.

The conventional athletes’ village has been replaced with local hotels, temporary wooden huts, and a cruise liner, which organisers say is safe, cost-effective and comfortable.

Between 4,000 and 5,000 athletes will stay on Italian cruise ship Costa Serena, which features 571 cabins, seven swimming pools, eight restaurants and nine bars. A further 2,000 athletes and officials will stay in wooden shipping container-style huts in Nagoya’s Garden Pier area while the rest will stay in hotels.

Why is there a growing accommodation crisis?

Athletes arriving in the industrial city have been met with an accommodation shortage , less than optimal conditions and an approaching typhoon.

Last week, hundreds of athletes were briefly evacuated from their accommodation as record rainfall lashed Nagoya . Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa said the extensive flooding left the athletes unharmed, adding: “We are not worried about the conditions of the venues, and we believe there is no problem holding the Asian Games as planned.”

But the accommodation crisis has gone from bad to worse in a matter of days. Complaints ranged from undersized beds and cramped conditions to male and female athletes being assigned the same room, which has led to the host Japan team looking at alternative arrangements.

Transportation mishaps have also been reported; South Korea’s men’s football team was taken to the baseball stadium instead, resulting in a 30-minute delay in their training session.

Local organisers have said the strain on accommodation arose because they were expecting 15,000 people – including athletes and officials – for the Games, but numbers increased to more than 17,000 as new sports were added.

Do the games serve as qualifiers for LA28?

Yes, the 2026 Asian Games double as a qualifying event for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics for a handful of sports.

In hockey, the winning men’s and women’s teams will directly qualify for the Olympic Games. Should they already qualify by winning the FIH Pro League, the spot will go to the next best team.

In squash, which makes its Olympic debut in 2028, the men’s and women’s gold medal winners qualify directly for one of 16 spots at the Olympics. Granted, the players must also feature in the Top 50 PSA rankings as of May 22, 2028.

The highest-ranked surfer per gender at the Asian Games will qualify for the Olympics through the continental quota.

Other sports which double as Olympic qualification include archery, sailing, tennis, and triathlon.

Which nation has been the most successful in Asian Games history?

China has been a dominant force at the games, topping the medal standings every year since 1982. At the Hangzhou 2023 games, the People’s Republic finished with 383 medals (201 gold, 111 silver, and 71 bronze).

That’s more than double the 188 medals won by second-place Japan, which has consistently shared a podium finish alongside South Korea.

Kazakhstan, Iran, India, Indonesia (host of the 2018 edition), Uzbekistan and Thailand have regularly finished in the top 10 medal standings.

articles.title: San Antonio FC embraces pressure of playoff hunt in road match against Sacramento
articles.summary: San Antonio midfielder Luke Haakenson says he and the team are primed to qualify for the playoffs with only six weeks left in the USL Championship season.
articles.body:
With San Antonio FC locked in a tight battle to qualify for the playoffs, midfielder Luke Haakenson is not letting the pressure get to him as the club prepares for its match against Sacramento Republic FC on Sunday.

"These are the games that you want to play for, and these are the moments you want to be as a professional, where everything is riding on it," Haakenson said. "You want the pressure because there's everything in the world to play for and you live for these moments because when you have a little bit of success, it just feels so good because we know how much we sacrificed for the year to put ourselves in this position."

SAFC and Sacramento kick off their match from Heart Health Park in Sacramento at 6 p.m.

The match comes at a critical time for both clubs with six weeks remaining in the USL Championship regular season. SAFC (9-6-9, 36 points) sits in seventh place in the USL Western Conference table, while Sacramento (9-5-9, 36 points) is fifth in the conference standings.

Over the last six weeks, the Western Conference table has been shifting. San Antonio was in second place in the standings before hitting a tough stretch in which it has only won once in its last five league matches.

Instead of fighting for one of the top four spots in the table, SAFC is now hanging on just to be one of the top eight finishers to qualify for the playoffs. Right now, just three points separate SAFC from going below the playoff line, where Phoenix Rising FC (8-7-9, 33 points) sits in ninth place.

Other clubs battling it out for playoff positioning are FC Tulsa (10-7-6, 36 points), which is in fourth place, and Orange County SC (9-6-9, 36 points) in sixth place.

Coming off a 2-1 loss to third-place Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC (11-9-4, 37 points) on the road last Friday, SAFC squares off against a Sacramento club which is 2-0-3 in its previous games, including a 1-0 win over Detroit City FC at home last week.

In its first match against Sacramento in May, SAFC edged out the Republic 2-1 at Toyota Field.

Defense has been the calling card for Sacramento recently with four clean sheets since Aug. 1. The Republic has conceded three goals combined in seven matches during that span.

"As a team, they defend really well, whether they play with five in the back or with four," Llamosa said. "They're a really good, organized team and obviously for us, this game or any other game, is not to concede early goals. Especially those kinds of teams that defend well because of the lead, especially at home, it's going to be tough to break them down."

Llamosa said SAFC will need to find a balance in how it plays against the Republic on its home turf.

"Their games are being close, but we have to consider they have really good forwards," Llamosa said. "So, we have to be very cautious about how we're going to attack and how we're going to prevent counterattacks, especially with those guys they have up front. So, if we can take advantage of that situation when they move the lines forward and give us the space, make sure when we're in a counterattack, we're smarter and create chances and score goals."

Haakenson is confident SAFC has the playmakers to counteract the talent Sacramento has on its squad, even if the Republic should score an early goal first.

"Honestly, I look at the quality we have in difference makers all over the field," Haakenson said. "So, I'm not worried about them scoring goals early because I know they'll be thinking the same thing about us. If you look at our attacking positions, we have guys who can make a play from wing back."

After enduring a tough stretch of the schedule in which SAFC played three games within six days, Llamosa said his squad should be ready for Sacramento on seven days of rest.

"It feels good to finally have a whole week before a game in Sacramento," Llamosa said. "That way we prepare better . . . guys reenergized after three games in six days."

With the season winding down and SAFC fighting tooth and nail to get into the postseason, backup goalkeeper Daniel Namani said the players have approached the training sessions like a game.

"So, we are treating, even the sessions here, as finals," Namani said. "We're being very competitive and translating that into game days. So, absolutely, each match we're treating it like a cup final but I think it starts here at training first. So, when it comes to game day, we're waiting for those moments. I think we'll be ready for those."

articles.title: Texas Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian denies The Athletic report on $55 million payroll
articles.summary: The Athletic reports that Texas football is among the highest-paying programs in the country with a payroll up to $55 million. Not true, said Steve Sarkisian...
articles.body:
Earlier this week, The Athletic listed the Texas Longhorns as one of the highest-paying programs in college football with a payroll of approximately $45-55 million.

But "that is inaccurate," Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian said during his Thursday weekly Zoom session with reporters.

"I think The Athletic and different outlets, I guess, do valuations on players of what they think players are worth and/or not worth," Sarkisian said.

According to The Athletic, which is owned by The New York Times Company, the outlet "worked to get as many independent, trustworthy estimates as possible from people inside and outside a program: those who broker the deals, direct the teams from the sidelines on Saturdays and watch the games from luxury boxes."

The Athletic also stated that it contacted at least one employee from each school "to give them an opportunity to offer information about their roster budgets."

The reporters' research estimated that Texas, Ohio State and Oregon had the most money available for player payment this season among all Power Four conference schools and Notre Dame. Ohio State had an estimated $49-54 million while Oregon boasted an estimated $48-54 million, joining Texas at the top of the list.

Eleven of the top 20 spenders are in the SEC, compared to six in the Big Ten.

But to Sarkisian's point about the inaccuracies of estimations, none of the available funds for players is public information. Sarkisian, who spent three seasons of his 26-year coaching career in the NFL, says he would support publicly releasing salaries if everyone followed the same disclosure rules, like teams do in professional sports.

"I'm all for it if everybody wants to submit all of their contracts to a general source like you do in the NFL, and everybody has access to the contracts, how they're written, how much each player's making, what are his bonus structures, so on and so forth," he said. "But I think we've got to be cautious in that if that's not what we're doing, and we're just making subjective guess-timations, then we take them as reality. I think that's the part that's a little bit disappointing."

Sarkisian's salary – he makes $10.8 million this season – along with that of every other coach at a public university is public. But Sarkisian said that until players' salaries are also public, "we've got to move with a little bit more caution to take everything as true."

"We're really the only ones that know what our roster's worth, and LSU only knows what their roster's worth, or Ohio State, Oregon, so on and so forth," he said. "What is everybody's roster worth or not worth? I think that's where we have to move with a little bit more caution and discretion."

articles.title: Sports ministry reaches out to Indian diaspora in Japan amid Asian Games lodging crisis
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: With the accommodation crisis at the Asian Games showing little sign of easing, the sports ministry has reached out to the Indian diaspora .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the accommodation crisis at the Asian Games showing little sign of easing, the sports ministry has reached out to the Indian diaspora in Nagoya for help in housing athletes if the shortage of rooms persists during the continental showpiece."Sports ministry has formed a three layer plan to deal with the issue. First layer involves officials at the airport; second involves booking more rooms, and the third involves liasoning with the Indian diaspora. These activities are being done by officials of the sports ministry, the team on the ground, Sports Authority of India and the Chef de Mission (Sehdev Yadav)," said a source tracking developments.Several athletes, including members of the Indian contingent, have complained about delays in being allotted accommodation. With no dedicated athletes' village, participants have been housed across container-style units, a docked cruise ship and hotels as organisers look to cut costs.Sahdev Yadav said on Friday that around 35 Indian athletes had already been moved to hotels after they failed to get their designated accommodation from the organisers. The situation could become more challenging as additional Indian athletes arrive in Nagoya according to their competition schedules."The sports ministry has reached out to the Indian diaspora to be on standby to help with the accommodation of its athletes in case there is shortage of rooms for them during the course of the Asian Games," a ministry official added.A senior sports ministry official said the Indian Embassy had played a key role in reaching out to around 2,000 Indian families in Nagoya. Several families have offered assistance should the accommodation shortage worsen.The accommodation arrangements have come in for criticism from several participating countries, with South Korea among the most vocal in questioning the organisation of the Games.The OCA, however, has rejected the criticism, saying attempts were being made on social media to exploit the situation and politicise the event.Nearly 11,000 athletes are expected to compete across 43 sports at the Asian Games, which run until October 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Astros are quietly dangerous in American League pennant race
articles.summary: The Astros could make some noise in the AL postseason.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros have been a .500 team or slightly below for most of the season.

That's why it's hard to believe they have a chance to earn an automatic berth to the ALDS if they win the AL West and finish with a top-two record in the American League.

This season, the AL West has been by far the worst division of the six. Not one of the five clubs has a positive run differential.

Houston's -50 run differential is the sixth-worst in the AL. Still, they have a solid chance to make a deep postseason run, ESPN's David Schoenfield wrote.

"The starting pitching makes that scenario a little less plausible, although we should point out that the rotation has a 3.15 ERA in September (fourth in the majors) with Hunter Brown and Hayden Wesneski both pitching well," Schoenfield wrote. "Even Cristian Javier has now had three good starts in a row. And Peter Lamber has been the one consistent and healthy starter throughout the season for the Astros."

Schoenfield notes that Houston's rotation should be its biggest concern going into the postseason.

It helps to have a dominant closer like Josh Hader and the frontrunner for AL MVP ( Yordan Alvarez ) in your lineup.

"So let's see: dominant closer, the best hitter in the game this season, power, and a rotation that has been mostly awful all season but is peaking at the right time. Consider yourself warned," Schoenfield added.

Based on the Astros' body of work in the regular season, it's hard to truly feel confident about their postseason chances.

But this is the same organization that went to seven consecutive AL Championship Series from 2017-23.
